items.title: Path of Valheiman DB
items.text:
A datamined reference for Path of Valheiman, the Path of Exile–inspired passive tree, crafting and loot overhaul for Valheim.

Every page here is generated from the mod's own files. The text is produced by the game's own code, so it matches what you see in game and updates with each patch.

Planning a build?

To plan your own build or explore builds shared by other players, head to povbuilds.com, the Path of Valheiman build planner.

items.title: Passive tree
items.text:
• Passive Tree Viewer: the full tree, searchable
  • Keystones: build-defining passives with a drawback
  • Notables: the larger passives, by category
  • Masteries: passives where you choose one option

items.title: Crafting
items.text:
• Craft Tree Viewer: the craft tree, with sectors and professions
  • Professions: each profession and its notables
  • Craft Notables and Craft Masteries
  • Buildings: the mod's kiln, rune carver table, gate, vacuum chest and wild sowing

items.title: Items
items.text:
• Mods: every property an item can roll, with tiers and weights
  • Item bases: weapons, armour, shields and trinkets, with stats and recipes
  • Currency: runes, essences, sigils and crafting materials
  • Jewels: base and unique jewels, and the properties base jewels roll
  • Uniques: unique jewels and belts, with their lines and where they drop

items.title: Monsters
items.text:
• Monster Modifiers: what starred creatures can roll, with their values
  • Bosses: the mod's bosses, how to summon them and what every boss drops
  • Creatures: runic kin and the creatures of the Blight Mist

items.title: Mechanics
items.text:
• Creature scaling: level, health and damage, stars, difficulty, Monster Power
  • Experience and levels: area and item levels, recommended player levels, experience fall-off
  • Loot and experience: what a kill drops and the experience it gives
  • Combat and building: critical strikes, evasion, resistances, enemy penetration, build cost

items.title: Patches
items.text: • Patches: what each update changed in the game data, compared with the version before

items.title: Keywords
items.text:
Underlined keywords link to their entry from the mod's in-game wiki, and show its definition on hover. Use the search bar to look up any passive or keyword.

Unimplemented content

The game files contain content that isn't finished yet, like placeholder passives or stats without proper text. It is listed here too, marked Unimplemented or Unfinished text.

items.title: Credits
items.text:
Path of Valheiman is made by treextr: mod page · Discord · Patreon · Boosty.

This is an unofficial fan site. All game data, names, text and node art belong to the mod author. This site does not host or redistribute the mod. Get it from the official page.

items.title: How it works
items.text: The mod ships its passive tree, craft tree, loot tables and translations as data embedded in its DLL. This site reads that data and generates every page from it. There is no manual data entry.

items.title: Ascendancy
items.text: An Ascendancy class makes your path your own: a small tree of its own beside the passive tree. Each path has its classes, and the altar at the end of a Halls of Oaths run offers the classes of your path.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
A class tree has 8 points; each small or notable node costs one, and a node must connect back to the class's start. The points come from the Halls of Oaths: 2 for each tier of gates whose final boss you defeat, once per character, up to 8.

With no class nodes taken, any completed halls altar lets you change your class within your path; your points stay. Refunding a class node costs 5 times a passive point's refund.

Classes marked early access are opened through PoV Link; the others are open to everyone.

The classes are also drawn in circles around the passive tree, each on the side of its path.

Every class notable is also listed on one page.

items.title: Buildings
items.text:
The pieces Path of Valheiman adds to the Hammer and the Cultivator. Each is built on a Valheim piece, with the mod's own look, cost and use.

Name Effect Azurite Kiln Grinds azurite into dust Rune Carver Table The crafting station for the mod's own items: runes, punches, sigils, rings, belts... Inscription Gate A Runecarver's portal: inscribe which portal of the world it leads to. Shift + use: inscribe the link. Vacuum Chest Pulls finished goods from nearby smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills, and feeds them from its contents. Shift + wheel: radius. Shift + use: what to collect. Runic Chest Stores runes in dedicated slots and applies them to equipment Runic Anvil Runic crafting with alloys and glyphs. Spends the item's potential and azurite dust Wild Sowing Wild growth. Planted on cultivated ground.

Passives that change building in general (cheaper pieces, less rain wear, station range...) are on the craft tree.

Data from Path of Valheiman 6.0.12, extracted 2026-11-13.

items.title: Craft Masteries
items.text: Options you choose on mastery passives. Each option is listed once, with the number of tree nodes that offer it; open an option for its full description and where to find it.

items.title: Beekeeper
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Cosy Hives 3% increased hive filling speed per point of comfortHives fill faster the more comfort there is around them 12 Guard Bees Bees sting enemies near your hives 12 Hive Chain Harvesting a hive collects from neighbouring hives one after another, hive by hive along the chain, not by area 12 Honey Stores Hives you built hold 2 times as much honey 12 Swarm Split Once a day an own hive that is full, its honey not yet taken, has a 5% chance to yield a queen beeOnce a day a hive you built that is full, with its honey not yet taken, has a 5% chance to yield a queen bee 12 Wildflower Meadow Own hives fill 5% faster for every flowering plant nearby (dandelion, thistle, flax, barley), up to 50%Hives you built fill faster for every flowering plant growing nearby (dandelion, thistle, flax, barley) 12 Winter Hive Hives you built work in cold biomes 12

items.title: Builder
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Auto Doors Doors you build open as anyone approaches and close behind them 10 Careful Builder You cannot damage player-built pieces 10 Floor as Roof Floors you build are a full roof: what is under them stays dry, is sheltered from rain and counts as under a roof for fires, beds, rest and stations 10 Hugin's Flight {key.hugin}, with a building tool in hand, sends the sight aloft as Hugin: the body hovers in place and pieces are placed within building range of the raven, up to 30 m from the body; [Space] rises, [Ctrl] sinks, [Shift] flies faster, {key.hugin} again returnsWith a hammer or hoe in hand, press B to send your sight aloft like Odin's raven and build from the air while your body stays safe on the ground. The view flies up to 30 m from you; pieces are placed within your Building range of the view and still need a workbench in reach and your materials 10 Light Frame Pieces you built lose only 50% of the usual support 10 Nearby Chests (building) Building draws materials from nearby chests 10 No Bounds Build and remove pieces where building is forbidden: dungeons, boss altars, traders' camps and other no-build places 10 Open-Air Bench The bench works under open sky 10 Weatherproof Pieces you built take no damage from rain, water or waves 10

items.text: Option Effect Nodes Any Soil Planted growth grows in any biome. items.text: Option Effect Nodes Cuttings Picking a wild plant has a 6% chance to give its seed; wild plants are sown only from their seedsForaging a wild plant has a 6% chance to give its seed. items.title: Pathfinder
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Field Portal You can build and dismantle portals without a workbench 13 Grave Tether When you die, your equipped gear, hotbar and food slots stay on you, and your grave is marked on the map until it is emptied 13 Momentum Slide Crouch while running fast or right after landing a jump to slide along the ground, keeping your speed. 13 Night Walker Every at Night bonus, combat and crafting alike, also works in the evening 13 Pull-Up Hold jump and push toward a wall while in the air to pull yourself up onto a ledge within reach. A pull-up costs 15 stamina, a low ledge half as much. A short tap of jump near a wall stays a wall rebound. 13 Quick Mark Shift + Y marks what you are looking at on your map with its own icon and name 13 Shared Map Standing near another player, you exchange explored map and pins with them 13 Sleep by the Fire You can sleep sitting at a fire: no bed and no roof needed, and the night passes even if someone on the server has not lain down 13 Sliding Down a Slope Crouched on a slope, the character rides down faster than running. 13 Trail Runner Running on a trail or a paved road costs 25% less staminaRunning on a trail costs 25% less stamina 13

items.title: Relic seeker
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Belt Lantern The Dvergr lantern hangs on your belt in its own equipment slot 11 Breadcrumbs Inside a dungeon the minimap draws the corridors you have walked, in the game's own map style 11 Chest Sight Chests in your view radius are marked on the map 11 Dungeon Sight Dungeon entrances within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap; the marks clear as soon as they leave that radius 11 Every Door Any door, built or in a dungeon, opens as you come up to it and closes behind you. A door with a key still needs the key in your bag. 11 Magic Purse A purse appears to the right of the inventory and collects your coins. Coins in the purse weigh nothing and are kept on death. 11 Return Path Once per dungeon, sitting down offers a flight to its exit for 3 surtling coresOnce per dungeon, sit down to fly to its exit for 3 surtling cores. If the dungeon is reset, the flight is available again. 11 Second Sweep Chests anywhere in the world that the character has emptied fully refill after a few in-game days, again and again, with fresh loot of their biome (Chest item quantity, Chest item rarity and Extra item apply). Aiming at such a chest shows the time left until it refills 11 Tidy Pack Two buttons in the bag: stack into nearby chests and sort the bag 11 Treasure Map Opening a chest has a 30% chance to mark the nearest unopened chest on the map; the mark goes once the chest is emptied 11

items.title: Runecarver
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Ascendant Rune +10% chance that a property added by a rune rises one tierWhen a rune adds or raises a property, it has a chance to rise one tier more as a separate step, beyond the item's level limit. You see a second flash, hear a chime and read "+1 affix tier". 12 Azurite Sight Azurite veins within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap: plain, corrupted and divine each with its own icon. A vein mined out by more than three quarters is no longer marked. 11 Chisel Quarrying Rune chisels also mine stone and ore deposits, like a pickaxe of the same metal: bronze, iron or black metal (flametal hits as hard as black metal). A deposit too hard for that pickaxe is too hard for the chisel. Chisel hits do not train the Pickaxes skill. Azurite veins are mined as before. 11 Divine Touch +2% chance for divine azuriteEach chisel hit on a plain azurite vein outside the mist has a chance to turn it divine, with the same lightning as a heavenly strike. Any chisel works, in any biome. 12 Inscription Gate You can build the Inscription Gate, a Runecarver portal with pink-violet runes. Shift + use on it opens the map of every portal in the world: pick one and inscribe the link, and everyone who enters the gate steps out there. 11 Last Touch Runic crafting can overspend an item's potential while any potential remains; the rest drops to zero. 11 Perfect Inscription +10% chance that a property rolled by a rune takes the highest value of its tierA property rolled by a rune (Fate included) has a chance to take the highest value of its tier. 12 Portal Crate Away from a workbench, dismantling a portal packs it into a crate that keeps its tag, author, durability and Inscription Gate link. Place it back from the crate anywhere. A crate cannot pass through a portal. 11 Relic Passage Dragon eggs for summoning, Hildir's chests and dvergr parts (charred cogwheels, dvergr needles, mechanical springs) go through portals, with no portal toll. Ore and metal are not included. 11 Runic Vise +1 capacity when crafting with runesOne more alloy or glyph slot at the Runic Anvil, on top of the anvil's own slots. 11 Vacuum Chest Unlocks the Vacuum Chest at the Rune Carver Table. It takes finished goods from smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills around it and feeds them from its contents. Shift + mouse wheel sets the radius, Shift + E the kind of goods it collects. 11

items.title: Shipwright
items.text: Option Effect Nodes Anchor Ships the character builds carry an anchor: anyone aiming at the helm drops or raises it with Shift+E. An anchored ship holds its place, still rocking on the waves and turning with the wind. 19 Deep Hold Ships you built carry one more row of cargo 19 Harbor Mark Your ships are marked on the map with a ship icon wherever they are 19 Mending at Sea Ships can be repaired with the hammer without a workbench nearby 19 Open Shipyard Ships can be built and taken apart with the hammer anywhere, without a workbench. Away from a workbench a ship is not broken into materials: it is packed into a crate together with its cargo, and the crate on the hotbar sets the same ship back on the water - with its hull, its builder, every shipwright property and everything that was in its hold. Nobody may stand aboard a ship being taken apart. 19 Salvage Float Nothing is lost to the sea: a ship's hold and items sunk in deep water float up in crates that stay put and are marked on the map until emptied 19 Storm Keel Ships you built keep full control in storms 19 Weather Sense The coming weather and when it arrives are shown under the minimap 19

items.title: Runic Forging
items.text: At the Runic Anvil a piece of equipment is reworked with alloys and glyphs. Every action spends the item's potential and azurite dust. Without a main glyph an action forges the item anew; alloys steer which properties it gets, glyphs change the item or the rules of the action. Alloys are smelted from special ores.

items.title: The anvil
items.text:
The Runic Anvil is built with the hammer near a workbench. Its stages open slots for alloys and glyphs (Runic Anvil: 1, Iron Vise: 2, Silver Matrix: 3); Runic Vise adds one of your own, up to 4 in all.

Its stock keeps alloys, glyphs, azurite dust and divine dust, one slot each with no limit: Ctrl+click moves one between the stock and the slots. Several players can use one anvil at once and see each other's choices.

items.title: Potential
items.text: Potential: every piece of equipment that can have a rarity has 65 at most, whatever its rarity; an item never worked at the anvil has it all. The prefix #% increased item potential raises the most: 65 × (1 + increase), rounded. The item remembers how much it has spent, so what is left follows the most when that prefix comes, goes or changes. Unique items, jewels other than base jewels, runes and items of fixed rarity have none. The item must be identified and not corrupted. Nothing restores spent potential.

items.title: Cost of an action
items.text:
An action at the anvil costs only the potential of the glyphs in it: alloys cost none, and an action with no glyph costs no potential. It also costs 30 Azurite Dust plus each alloy's and glyph's dust; valuable and very valuable glyphs also take Divine Azurite Dust. Dust comes from the anvil's stock first and the rest from your bag; alloys and glyphs come from the stock.

cost = ⌈glyphs × (1 − reduced cost)⌉, reduced cost at most 90%critical craft = ⌈cost ÷ 2⌉

A critical craft costs half the potential, rounded up. Its chance is 5%, plus the runic crafting nodes of the craft tree, which also reduce the cost.

With the Glyph of Delay, 30% of actions spend no potential at all; the critical craft is rolled only when that fails. Dust and the alloys and glyphs are spent either way.

An action needs its whole cost still left on the item. With Last Touch any potential left is enough, and the item ends at zero. At zero, runic crafting is closed; the item keeps working.

Alloys and glyphs (potential) Cost Critical craft Actions from full potential 3 3 2 21 5 5 3 13 10 10 5 6 20 20 10 3 35 35 18 1

items.title: Forging
items.text: An action without a main glyph forges the item: every prefix and suffix is replaced and the item becomes rare (rarity) with 3 prefixes and 3 suffixes. A sealed property stays. The properties that fit the item must be enough for a full forging. Alloys work only here.

items.title: How alloys weight the roll
items.text:
Each alloy favours the properties of its theme. For the item on the anvil the game takes the share s of the forge pool's weight those properties hold, and multiplies their weight so that they come to about 35% of the rolls:

× = 0.35 × (1 − s) ÷ (0.65 × s), at least ×5, at most ×25 Theme's share of the pool Multiplier Share with the alloy 1% ×25 20.16% 2% ×25 33.78% 5% ×10.23 35% 10% ×5 35.71% 20% ×5 55.56% 40% ×5 76.92%

A property in the themes of several alloys adds their multipliers: 1 + (×₁ − 1) + (×₂ − 1)…, so at least ×9 with two alloys and ×13 with three (×5 each).

Glyph of the Depths: properties of weight 300 or less, the rare ones, are ×3 as likely, on top of the alloys.

An alloy with no property for this item cannot be used: the anvil says so and nothing is spent. The Forge button's tooltip shows each alloy's share before and after.

items.title: Glyph rules
items.text:
One main glyph per action replaces forging with its own change. Support glyphs change how an action rolls or what it costs:

Glyph Kind Works with Effect Glyph of Brokkr Main instead of forging +1 permanent quality; existing properties are kept Glyph of Three Knots Support forging Forging gives 4 properties instead of 6, one fewer on each side; the best available tier is twice as likely Glyph of the Norns Support forging, Glyph of Tempering, Glyph of the Last Heat Property values are rolled twice within their tier, the better roll is kept Glyph of the Depths Support forging Rare properties are three times as likely Glyph of Echo Support any action 35% chance to keep each other alloy and glyph of the action; this glyph is always spent Glyph of the Void Main instead of forging 25% chance to add a phantom socket beyond the item's socket limit Glyph of Memory Support forging Forging keeps one random existing property Unbinding Glyph of Prefixes Main instead of forging Removes one random prefix Unbinding Glyph of Suffixes Main instead of forging Removes one random suffix Glyph of Cleansing Main instead of forging Removes all prefixes and suffixes; everything else on the item is kept Sifting Glyph Main instead of forging Removes one property of the weakest tier Glyph of Tempering Main instead of forging One random property rises one tier Glyph of the Last Heat Main instead of forging 50%: every property rises one tier. Otherwise all remaining potential burns out Glyph of Delay Support any action 30% chance not to spend the action's potential Glyph of Ascension Main instead of forging +5 item level, up to the supported limit Reinforcing Glyph Main instead of forging Maximum durability ×1.25, again with every use; wear is kept as a share
  • Glyph of Echo: each other alloy and glyph of the action is kept at 35%; the Echo itself is always spent. It needs another alloy or glyph.
  • Glyph of the Void: 25% chance of a phantom socket; the cost is paid either way. The item must be able to have sockets.
  • Glyph of the Last Heat: 50% chance that every property that can rise a tier does; otherwise all the item's remaining potential burns away.
  • Glyph of Ascension: +5 item level, up to 246, the Deep North's level.
  • Reinforcing Glyph: maximum durability ×1.25 with each use (counted up to 40 uses); the item keeps its share of durability.
  • Glyph of Three Knots: forging gives 2 prefixes and 2 suffixes; the best tier the item can reach is ×2 as likely.
  • Glyph of Memory: forging keeps one random property of the item.
  • Sifting Glyph: removes a property of the weakest tier, a random one among equals.
  • A sealed property is never removed or changed; the Glyph of Cleansing is refused on an item that has one.

items.title: What is refused
items.text:
The anvil checks an action before anything is paid. When one of these applies, the action is refused with its reason and nothing is spent:

  • Only one main glyph per action
  • Each alloy and glyph can be used once per action
  • Not enough open slots on this anvil
  • Alloys only change forging; remove them or the main glyph
  • … has no properties to favour on this item
  • This glyph only works with forging
  • The Glyph of the Norns needs an action that rolls property values
  • The Glyph of Echo needs another alloy or glyph to keep
  • The Glyph of Memory needs a property to keep
  • This item has no potential left
  • Not enough potential: … needed, … left
  • Unique items cannot be crafted with runes
  • This item cannot be crafted with runes
  • This item cannot become rare
  • Not enough properties fit this item for a full forging
  • This item cannot have sockets
  • No property can rise a tier at this item level
  • The item is already at the highest item level
  • This item has no durability
  • A sealed property cannot be removed
  • Jewels have no quality
  • Quality does nothing on utility items

items.title: Phantom socket
items.text: The Glyph of the Void may open a phantom socket beyond the item's usual limit of sockets. It takes what an ordinary socket takes and stays through punches, reforging and repairs.

items.title: Open Shipyard
items.text: Craft mastery option · Shipwright

items.title: Description
items.text:
What the game shows when you hover the option, alongside the effect above.

Ships can be built and taken apart with the hammer anywhere, without a workbench. Away from a workbench a ship is not broken into materials: it is packed into a crate together with its cargo, and the crate on the hotbar sets the same ship back on the water - with its hull, its builder, every shipwright property and everything that was in its hold. Nobody may stand aboard a ship being taken apart.

Nobody may be aboard during packing. Dismantle with the hammer ([Mouse 3]); to deploy, select the crate on the hotbar and place the ship like any build piece. The crate goes through portals while its hold carries nothing a portal refuses.

items.title: Mastery options
items.text: Option Effect Anchor Ships the character builds carry an anchor: anyone aiming at the helm drops or raises it with Shift+E. Away from a workbench a ship is not broken into materials: it is packed into a crate together with its cargo, and the crate on the hotbar sets the same ship back on the water - with its hull, its builder, every shipwright property and everything that was in its hold. items.text:
Craft notable · Table · Shipwright · Show on tree

10% increased ship speed

items.title: Mastery options
items.text: Option Effect Anchor Ships the character builds carry an anchor: anyone aiming at the helm drops or raises it with Shift+E. An anchored ship holds its place, still rocking on the waves and turning with the wind. Open Shipyard Ships can be built and taken apart with the hammer anywhere, without a workbench. Away from a workbench a ship is not broken into materials: it is packed into a crate together with its cargo, and the crate on the hotbar sets the same ship back on the water - with its hull, its builder, every shipwright property and everything that was in its hold. Nobody may stand aboard a ship being taken apart. Mending at Sea Ships can be repaired with the hammer without a workbench nearby Salvage Float Nothing is lost to the sea: a ship's hold and items sunk in deep water float up in crates that stay put and are marked on the map until emptied Storm Keel Ships you built keep full control in storms Harbor Mark Your ships are marked on the map with a ship icon wherever they are Deep Hold Ships you built carry one more row of cargo Weather Sense The coming weather and when it arrives are shown under the minimap

+5% chance for divine socket

items.title: Mastery options
items.text: Option Effect Inscription Gate You can build the Inscription Gate, a Runecarver portal with pink-violet runes. Shift + use on it opens the map of every portal in the world: pick one and inscribe the link, and everyone who enters the gate steps out there. Azurite Sight Azurite veins within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap: plain, corrupted and divine each with its own icon. A vein mined out by more than three quarters is no longer marked. Divine Touch +2% chance for divine azuriteEach chisel hit on a plain azurite vein outside the mist has a chance to turn it divine, with the same lightning as a heavenly strike. Any chisel works, in any biome. Ascendant Rune +10% chance that a property added by a rune rises one tierWhen a rune adds or raises a property, it has a chance to rise one tier more as a separate step, beyond the item's level limit. You see a second flash, hear a chime and read "+1 affix tier". Perfect Inscription +10% chance that a property rolled by a rune takes the highest value of its tierA property rolled by a rune (Fate included) has a chance to take the highest value of its tier. Portal Crate Away from a workbench, dismantling a portal packs it into a crate that keeps its tag, author, durability and Inscription Gate link. Place it back from the crate anywhere. A crate cannot pass through a portal. Relic Passage Dragon eggs for summoning, Hildir's chests and dvergr parts (charred cogwheels, dvergr needles, mechanical springs) go through portals, with no portal toll. Ore and metal are not included. Vacuum Chest Unlocks the Vacuum Chest at the Rune Carver Table. It takes finished goods from smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills around it and feeds them from its contents. Shift + mouse wheel sets the radius, Shift + E the kind of goods it collects. Chisel Quarrying Rune chisels also mine stone and ore deposits, like a pickaxe of the same metal: bronze, iron or black metal (flametal hits as hard as black metal). A deposit too hard for that pickaxe is too hard for the chisel. Chisel hits do not train the Pickaxes skill. Azurite veins are mined as before. Last Touch Runic crafting can overspend an item's potential while any potential remains; the rest drops to zero. Runic Vise +1 capacity when crafting with runesOne more alloy or glyph slot at the Runic Anvil, on top of the anvil's own slots.

Carry weight
items.text:
Craft notable · Beast · Runecarver · Show on tree

+30 carry weight

items.title: Mastery options
items.text: Option Effect Inscription Gate You can build the Inscription Gate, a Runecarver portal with pink-violet runes. Shift + use on it opens the map of every portal in the world: pick one and inscribe the link, and everyone who enters the gate steps out there. Azurite Sight Azurite veins within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap: plain, corrupted and divine each with its own icon. A vein mined out by more than three quarters is no longer marked. Divine Touch +2% chance for divine azuriteEach chisel hit on a plain azurite vein outside the mist has a chance to turn it divine, with the same lightning as a heavenly strike. Any chisel works, in any biome. Ascendant Rune +10% chance that a property added by a rune rises one tierWhen a rune adds or raises a property, it has a chance to rise one tier more as a separate step, beyond the item's level limit. You see a second flash, hear a chime and read "+1 affix tier". Perfect Inscription +10% chance that a property rolled by a rune takes the highest value of its tierA property rolled by a rune (Fate included) has a chance to take the highest value of its tier. Portal Crate Away from a workbench, dismantling a portal packs it into a crate that keeps its tag, author, durability and Inscription Gate link. Place it back from the crate anywhere. A crate cannot pass through a portal. Relic Passage Dragon eggs for summoning, Hildir's chests and dvergr parts (charred cogwheels, dvergr needles, mechanical springs) go through portals, with no portal toll. Ore and metal are not included. Vacuum Chest Unlocks the Vacuum Chest at the Rune Carver Table. It takes finished goods from smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills around it and feeds them from its contents. Shift + mouse wheel sets the radius, Shift + E the kind of goods it collects. Chisel Quarrying Rune chisels also mine stone and ore deposits, like a pickaxe of the same metal: bronze, iron or black metal (flametal hits as hard as black metal). A deposit too hard for that pickaxe is too hard for the chisel. Chisel hits do not train the Pickaxes skill. Azurite veins are mined as before. Last Touch Runic crafting can overspend an item's potential while any potential remains; the rest drops to zero. Runic Vise +1 capacity when crafting with runesOne more alloy or glyph slot at the Runic Anvil, on top of the anvil's own slots.

items.title: Tanner
items.text: Profession · Beast

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 184 1 5 Fibres gather under a practiced hand, and an extra length of thread winds onto the spool. The same care gives leather gear a lasting life. Hide and wood are measured twice before the knife falls. Nothing useful is left among the offcuts. 631 2 4 Hide and sinew are measured twice by lamplight, and every offcut is saved. The awl flies across coat and bow alike; patient seams and well-seasoned wood make gear fit to endure many winters. 1,887 3 2 Now and then a bow or coat leaves the bench finer than its pattern. Such work is remembered long after its maker. 3,175 4 3 Layers of hide overlap like a beast’s winter coat. Craft XP Stage Area Lore 55 1 1 A humble straw skep hums at the meadow's edge. Patient keepers sometimes find a second queen stirring among the comb, ready to found a new hive. 184 2 2 Bees swarm in the warm hour after rain. Keepers who listen to the hive know when a young queen is about to rise from the brood. 547 3 4 Golden comb drips thick in the late summer sun. Honey from these hives fills the jars to the brim and sits heavy and sweet in a hungry belly. 908 4 3 Deep in the clover fields the hives divide and multiply. Each new queen carries the old colony's blessing into another skep. 1,594 5 7 The hives here never seem to sleep. Bees drone from first light to dusk, and the honey flows faster and more freely than elsewhere. 2,215 6 8 Old skeps stand in rows like the halls of a small kingdom. Honey overflows the combs, and young queens rise to rule new swarms. 3,726 8 6 The bees here work as if Odin himself awaits his mead. Comb fills quickly, and the hive repays its keeper sooner than seems natural. 4,969 9 5 At the meadow's heart stands a hive older than any rune-stone, and its bees never rest. Honey runs from it as swiftly as a spring thaw. This honey is said to be gathered from the flowers at Yggdrasil's roots. A single spoonful warms the blood and sustains a warrior through long marches.

The seeker who reaches this far leaves with a heavier pack. Pitch-soaked rags and a well-trimmed wick. The delver's light reaches further into the dark and refuses to go out.

items.title: Areas and stages

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 86 1 2 Raspberries in the meadows, mushrooms under the birches. A sharp-eyed forager often finds a second cluster hiding behind the first. 306 2 7 The forest feeds those who know where to look. Baskets fill with extra berries and woven bags hold more of nature's bounty. Wild greens grow back where they were picked, and the forager's hands snatch berries from further away. The woods are generous here. 908 3 4 In the shadow of old pines, mushrooms grow in thick rings. A forager who knows the spot comes back with twice the haul. 1,535 4 5 Picked thistle and bramble sprout anew with unusual haste. Old foragers knew the right way to leave a bush so it would bloom again. 2,681 5 6 A broad sweep of the hand gathers a whole patch at once. Berries and herbs from all around fall into the forager's basket. 3,726 6 1 Deep in the Black Forest, the ground is thick with plenty. Each bush seems to give a little more than it should. 4,969 7 3 Sturdy baskets and deep pouches. The master forager returns from the woods heavily laden with everything the land offers.

Silver from the mountain feels lighter in the miner's pack. 2,940 1 6 A pick loosens an extra fragment from the vein. A sturdy pack and a steady back carry the mountain’s bounty home. 3,726 8 4 The mountain's heart yields to heavy blows. Each strike tears more ore loose than the last. 4,969 9 5 At the roots of the world, where the Dvergr once delved, cracks open all over the stone. Old masters could see every flaw in the vein.

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:
Each area of the profession on the craft tree can be revealed once you have earned enough craft XP in the profession. Your profession stage is the highest stage among the areas you have reached.

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 55 1 1 A wayfarer's first lessons: leap without tiring, swim without drowning. Rivers and stones barely slow the path ahead. 184 2 2 A crackling campfire under the open sky. A wanderer finds true rest by its warmth, far from any hall. 547 3 8 Light boots and a long stride. Swift travellers cover the leagues between the meadows and the mountains before nightfall. Smoke rises from a ring of stones beside the trail. A seasoned traveller makes the wild a home with a single fire. 908 4 4 Stories by the fire and a pelt to sleep on. The road is long, but the wayfarer's camps grant a comfort like that of a mead hall. 2,215 6 3 A fall from a cliff is but a stumble to a seasoned wayfarer. And when death comes, the path back to the corpse is run with renewed vigour. Swift legs and a lofty leap carry the wayfarer over hill and stream. With each journey, the unknown map unfolds a little wider. 2,929 7 7 Old runes etched in stones and ruins call out from afar. Experienced travellers can sense their glow long before they reach them. 3,726 8 6 From every ridge, the wayfarer sees for miles. The fog of uncharted lands melts away before a wise traveller's gaze. 4,969 9 5 Even Valhalla's gate cannot hold back a true wayfarer. After death, they race back to reclaim their gear, swift and fearless.

items.title: Areas and stages
items.text:

Craft XP Stage Area Lore 55 1 6 Oak ribs and pine planks promise a voyage with a full hold. A shipwright bears the supplies with ease and shapes hulls that cut swiftly through the waves. 184 2 8 Taut sails catch the wind while a well-shaped keel answers every touch of the helm. Ships raised in this yard run swift and turn sure; from the prow, a watchful sailor finds distant shores and a safe way through the waves. 547 3 3 Many voyages teach the feel of the sea. The skilled helmsman catches every breath of wind and steers through narrow straits with ease. 908 4 7 An old boathouse lies shrouded in mist. The secrets of the shipwrights who built here are known only to the tides. 1,594 5 1 Sailors whisper prayers to Njord before the voyage. On these waters, the wind so often blows from behind. 2,929 7 2 Fast ships and strong swimmers. items.title: Aftershock
items.text: A second eruption at a slam's point a moment later, with the slam's own damage and its own modifiers. It is rolled once per slam, not per enemy hit, and never makes another aftershock.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Slam: the sledge's area swing counts (Valheim's other area attacks don't), and so does an alternative attack Ground Strike turns into one: it uses the weapon's own area radius, or 3 m if the weapon has no area attack. Your area of effect widens a slam's radius.

A slam's slash and pierce damage, after their own conversions, is dealt as blunt at 50%; the rest of it is lost. Its blunt, elemental and other damage stay whole, and its blunt (with what slash and pierce added to it) converts as usual. Slash and pierce gained as extra fold into blunt the same way. Flat damage that applies to slams or area hits but not to the weapon's other hits is added to it as blunt.

Aftershock: rolled once per slam, at most 100%. 0.45 s later it erupts at the slam's point, in the slam's radius widened by the area increases that work with its aftershocks and not with the slam itself, and hits everything there with the slam's full damage. An aftershock never rolls another, though repeat chance can make it erupt once more.

An aftershock pushes enemies away from where it erupts.

A thrown club, mace or sledge that lands on the ground (not on a creature) slams there once: 3 m × your area of effect, with 100% of the weapon's damage × your skill multiplier, against every enemy and object in it. A thrown sceptre that lands casts its spell there instead.

A charged attack that isn't a slam can make aftershocks too, from aftershock chance that works with charged attacks: each full 100% gives one, and the rest is a chance for one more, each 0.45 s after the last, where the enemy was hit, in the weapon's area radius or 3 m, whichever is larger, × your area increases that work with aftershocks of that attack.

Primary attacks that are slams: Demolisher, Frostfire Sledge, Iron Sledge, Nord Sledge, Stagbreaker, Thunderblood Sledge, Wooden Sledge.

Alternative attacks that Ground Strike turns into slams: Battleaxe, Berserkir Axes, Black Metal Atgeir, Black Metal Battleaxe, Bleeding Berserkir Axes, Bronze Atgeir, Brutal Slayer, Crystal Battleaxe, Demolisher, Early Axes, Frostfire Atgeir, Frostfire Greataxe, Frostfire Greatsword, Frostfire Sledge, Himminafl, Iron Atgeir, Iron Sledge, Krom, Nord Atgeir, Nord Greataxe, Nord Greatsword, Nord Sledge, Primal Berserkir Axes, Primal Slayer, Scourging Slayer, Skull Splittur, Slayer, Stagbreaker, Thunderblood Atgeir, Thunderblood Greataxe, Thunderblood Greatsword, Thunderblood Sledge, Thundering Berserkir Axes, Wooden Atgeir, Wooden Battleaxe, Wooden Greatsword, Wooden Sledge.

items.title: Ailments and resistances
items.text:
Matching damage is required to build an ailment. Build-up improves application, ailment damage improves damage over time, and duration changes how long the effect lasts; resistances protect against incoming damage.

Data from Path of Valheiman 6.0.12, extracted 2026-11-13.

items.title: Ailment damage
items.text: Increases damage over time from bleeding, burning and poison, separately from the damage of the hit that caused them. It does not affect chill. Old shock-damage bonuses now act as shock effect.

items.title: How it works
items.text: Ailment: each comes from the matching part of your hits' damage, as the enemy takes it after its resistances and armour: bleeding from slash, burning from fire, poison from poison, chill from frost and shock from lightning. Burning and shock roll against layers that recent hits leave on the enemy, bleeding and poison roll a chance on every hit, and chill fills a gauge.

items.title: Burning and shock: layers
items.text:
Flammability left by a hit = 20% × fire damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up) × more Conductivity left by a hit = 25% × lightning damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up) × more

Every fire hit leaves a layer of flammability on the enemy and every lightning hit a layer of conductivity, each for 8 s. The hit then ignites or shocks with a chance equal to all of that kind's layers on the enemy, its own included, at most 100%, plus your flat chance to ignite or shock × (1 + build-up) × more. Base health is the enemy's maximum health without the mod's difficulty scaling.

The layer one hit leaves, by its damage as a share of the enemy's base health:

Damage ÷ base health 5% 10% 25% 50% Flammability, +0% build-up 1.6% 3.2% 8% 16% Flammability, +100% build-up 3.2% 6.4% 16% 32% Conductivity, +0% build-up 2% 4% 10% 20% Conductivity, +100% build-up 4% 8% 20% 40%

A tarred enemy counts 30% more flammability (layers and tar together at most 100%); on a wet enemy each flammability layer is × 0.5.

Ground Effects that burn or shock add layers the same way and apply their ailment once the enemy's layers reach 50%.

items.title: Bleeding and poison: chance
items.text:
chance = flat chance × (1 + build-up) × more

Every hit with slash or poison damage rolls its chance to bleed or poison; how much damage the hit deals doesn't change the chance. There is no base chance: it comes from flat chance to bleed or poison and flat ailment chance, which build-up raises.

A hit bleeds at most once. For poison, every full 100% of chance applies one poison for certain and the rest is the chance of one more, each from the hit's poison damage.

With a stat that lets pierce damage bleed, 50% of the hit's pierce damage counts as slash for bleeding.

items.title: Chill: the gauge
items.text:
gauge filled by a hit = frost damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up)

How much of the gauge one hit fills, by its damage as a share of the enemy's base health:

Damage ÷ base health 5% 10% 25% 50% Filled, +0% build-up 8% 16% 40% 80% Filled, +100% build-up 16% 32% 80% 100%

At 100% chill starts, from the strongest frost hit since the gauge began to fill. The gauge then stays full, so every further frost hit applies chill again from its own damage. 3 s after the last frost hit the gauge drains, 25% per second; chill ends when it is empty (at most 7 s after that hit).

A rune ward on the enemy doesn't lower the damage ailments count: they count the hit as if the ward weren't there (poison damage passes wards anyway). For bleeding, chill and shock, the extra damage the enemy takes from shock doesn't count.

items.title: What each ailment does
items.text:
• Bleeding: 20% of the slash damage per second for 4 s (80% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (physical). Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One bleed per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second.

    Melee hits with Gravedigger's Needle bleed for 7 s at base instead. - Burning: 25% of the igniting hit's fire damage per second for 4 s (100% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (fire); fire damage increases don't apply again. Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One burn per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second. A wet enemy burns out 6 times as fast.

    With Flame Without a Burial, your burning deals spirit damage instead of fire damage, × your damage over time multiplier for spirit. - Poison: 15% of the poison damage per second for 4 s (60% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (poison), plus any share of the enemy's base health your stats add, spread over the same 4 s (ailment damage doesn't raise that part). Longer duration adds seconds. Each poison runs on its own timer, and each player can keep 3 on an enemy (more with limit bonuses); past that, a new one replaces your weakest if it would deal more. Skeletons and the Charred take poison damage normally, but their chance to be poisoned is halved; summoned skeletons stay immune. - Chill: Valheim's frost effect, its strength × (1 + your general and chill ailment damage increases); ailment and status duration make it last longer. - Shock: for 3 s the enemy takes 20% increased damage from every source and builds up stagger faster by the same share. Shock effect raises it, at most 50%; the hit's damage doesn't change it. Only the strongest shock on an enemy acts, whoever applied it. Flat ailment damage does nothing for shock.

    shock = 20% × (1 + ailment effect and shock effect increases) × more, at most 50%

    Increases to shock's ailment damage count as shock effect. Ailment and status duration make it last longer.

Ailment damage multipliers for burning, poison and bleeding: × (1 + ailment damage increases, general and that ailment's) × their more multipliers; flat ailment damage adds its amount spread over 4 s. Each player's ailments tick on their own, once a second.

Damage over Time Speed: × (1 + its increases, general and that ailment's) × more, at least × 0.1. Burning, poison and bleeding deal their damage per second × that and end that much sooner, so the total stays the same.

With Deferred Doom, only critical strikes inflict ailments, and the damage over time of the ailments they inflict is × your critical strike multiplier.

Damage ÷ base health 5% 10% 25% 50% Flammability, +0% build-up 1.6% 3.2% 8% 16% Flammability, +100% build-up 3.2% 6.4% 16% 32% Conductivity, +0% build-up 2% 4% 10% 20% Conductivity, +100% build-up 4% 8% 20% 40%

A tarred enemy counts 30% more flammability (layers and tar together at most 100%); on a wet enemy each flammability layer is × 0.5.

Ground Effects that burn or shock add layers the same way and apply their ailment once the enemy's layers reach 50%.

items.title: Bleeding and poison: chance
items.text:
chance = flat chance × (1 + build-up) × more

Every hit with slash or poison damage rolls its chance to bleed or poison; how much damage the hit deals doesn't change the chance. There is no base chance: it comes from flat chance to bleed or poison and flat ailment chance, which build-up raises.

A hit bleeds at most once. For poison, every full 100% of chance applies one poison for certain and the rest is the chance of one more, each from the hit's poison damage.

With a stat that lets pierce damage bleed, 50% of the hit's pierce damage counts as slash for bleeding.

items.title: Chill: the gauge
items.text:
gauge filled by a hit = frost damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up)

How much of the gauge one hit fills, by its damage as a share of the enemy's base health:

Damage ÷ base health 5% 10% 25% 50% Filled, +0% build-up 8% 16% 40% 80% Filled, +100% build-up 16% 32% 80% 100%

At 100% chill starts, from the strongest frost hit since the gauge began to fill. The gauge then stays full, so every further frost hit applies chill again from its own damage. 3 s after the last frost hit the gauge drains, 25% per second; chill ends when it is empty (at most 7 s after that hit).

A rune ward on the enemy doesn't lower the damage ailments count: they count the hit as if the ward weren't there (poison damage passes wards anyway). For bleeding, chill and shock, the extra damage the enemy takes from shock doesn't count.

items.title: What each ailment does
items.text:
• Bleeding: 20% of the slash damage per second for 4 s (80% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (physical). Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One bleed per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second.

    Melee hits with Gravedigger's Needle bleed for 7 s at base instead. - Burning: 25% of the igniting hit's fire damage per second for 4 s (100% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (fire); fire damage increases don't apply again. Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One burn per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second. A wet enemy burns out 6 times as fast.

    With Flame Without a Burial, your burning deals spirit damage instead of fire damage, × your damage over time multiplier for spirit. - Poison: 15% of the poison damage per second for 4 s (60% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (poison), plus any share of the enemy's base health your stats add, spread over the same 4 s (ailment damage doesn't raise that part). Longer duration adds seconds. Each poison runs on its own timer, and each player can keep 3 on an enemy (more with limit bonuses); past that, a new one replaces your weakest if it would deal more. Skeletons and the Charred take poison damage normally, but their chance to be poisoned is halved; summoned skeletons stay immune. - Chill: Valheim's frost effect, its strength × (1 + your general and chill ailment damage increases); ailment and status duration make it last longer. - Shock: for 3 s the enemy takes 20% increased damage from every source and builds up stagger faster by the same share. Shock effect raises it, at most 50%; the hit's damage doesn't change it. Only the strongest shock on an enemy acts, whoever applied it. Flat ailment damage does nothing for shock.

    shock = 20% × (1 + ailment effect and shock effect increases) × more, at most 50%

    Increases to shock's ailment damage count as shock effect. Ailment and status duration make it last longer.

Ailment damage multipliers for burning, poison and bleeding: × (1 + ailment damage increases, general and that ailment's) × their more multipliers; flat ailment damage adds its amount spread over 4 s. Each player's ailments tick on their own, once a second.

Damage over Time Speed: × (1 + its increases, general and that ailment's) × more, at least × 0.1. Burning, poison and bleeding deal their damage per second × that and end that much sooner, so the total stays the same.

With Deferred Doom, only critical strikes inflict ailments, and the damage over time of the ailments they inflict is × your critical strike multiplier.

items.title: Area of effect
items.text: Increases the size or reach of supported attacks and effects. It does not increase their damage; area damage is separate. An area never reaches through walls: an explosion, a ground slam, a burst or a chain hits only those with nothing solid between them and its centre.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Area of effect widens attacks in a straight line: the factor multiplies the hit radius, not the ground it covers. +100% area doubles the radius and covers four times the ground.

radius × max(0.1, (1 + area increases) × area multipliers)

Area attacks (a slam is one) get the wider radius; other swings reach further as well.

Area hits of players and tamed creatures (area attacks, strikes, Smites, splashes, aftershocks, explosions and ground areas) reach only targets that no wall shields from the hit's centre.

items.title: Armour
items.text: Reduces damage remaining after block and resistances, before endurance and the rune shield. It absorbs a greater share of smaller hits; armour penetration ignores part of this protection.

items.title: Armour
items.text:
Armour is Valheim's own: it reduces each hit by the same share for all its damage types, much against small hits, less against big ones. With hit damage the sum of the hit's damage types:

armour < damage ÷ 2: damage taken = damage − armour; otherwise: damage taken = damage² ÷ (4 × armour) armour against creatures = your armour × 1.05 × (1 + armour effectiveness increases) − the creature's armour penetration

Armour applies after rune shield and block. Creatures ignore part of it: see enemy penetration. Damage taken, by armour and hit:

items.text:

Bosses move toward the next biome's values. Creatures with the Piercing modifier ignore more.

items.title: Ascension
items.text: A Lord's Brand ascends any piece of equipment to the biome after its boss. Weapons (pickaxes too), shields, armour and summoning staves: base damage (in the item's own damage types), durability, block and armour rise to that biome's items of the same kind and slot - nothing goes down; a summoning staff's minion becomes as strong as that biome's creatures. Equipment with nothing to compare - rings, belts, amulets, trinkets, utility items, capes without armour, other tools - gains only item level, unlocking higher property tiers on future rolls; its properties, implicit effects, base stats, durability and quality remain unchanged. One brand per item, and only upward.

items.title: Attributes
items.text: Strength raises health regeneration and carry weight; Dexterity raises stamina regeneration and evasion rating; Intelligence raises eitr regeneration and rune shield. Governing attributes also raise weapon damage through the skill multiplier.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Each point of an attribute gives:

Attribute Per point Per 100 points Strength 0.125% increased health regeneration+0.2 carry weight 12.5% increased health regeneration+20 carry weight Dexterity 0.185% increased stamina regeneration0.2% increased evasion rating 18.5% increased stamina regeneration20% increased evasion rating Intelligence 0.185% increased eitr regeneration+0.16 rune shield 18.5% increased eitr regeneration+16 rune shield

Weapons governed by attributes multiply their damage by a random skill multiplier, picked anew for every hit between its midpoint − 0.15 and + 0.15, never below 0. The midpoint grows with the weapon's governing attribute points (with two, their average); Valheim's own weapon skill level doesn't count.

midpoint = 0.4 × (1 + 1.5 × (points ÷ 300)^0.75) Points 0 50 100 200 300 500 Midpoint 0.4 0.56 0.66 0.84 1 1.28

Governing attributes by weapon skill:

Weapon skill Governing attributes Swords Strength, Intelligence Knives Intelligence, Dexterity Clubs Strength Polearms Strength, Intelligence Spears Dexterity, Strength Axes Dexterity, Strength Bows Dexterity Elemental Magic Intelligence Blood Magic Intelligence Fists Dexterity Pickaxes Strength Crossbows Dexterity, Strength

Sceptres are governed by Strength and Intelligence, whatever their skill.

items.title: Backstab
items.text: Extra damage against an enemy that has not noticed the attacker yet, regardless of attack direction. Weapons carry no backstab bonus of their own: it comes only from sneak attack damage bonuses.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
When the hit reaches an enemy, the increases that depend on it join the same sum:

  • increases against enemies of a kind or in a state (bosses, enemies with ailments and the like)
  • backstab: against an enemy that hasn't noticed you; Valheim's own backstab bonus is turned off
  • +15% while the enemy is staggered, instead of Valheim's double damage (stagger)
  • charged attack: +25%

Flat damage against the enemy (flat backstab damage, flat damage against enemies of a kind) goes to the hit's largest type, × your skill multiplier × (1 + the whole sum). It comes after the critical hit, so a crit doesn't multiply it.

Last come the increases and more multipliers that need something of the hit and something of the enemy together; the increases join the same sum.

Every step of a hit, in order: Order of a hit.

items.title: Biome level
items.text: Experience from a biome decreases as the character outlevels it. This depends on the biome rather than the enemy; direct passive-point rewards are unaffected.

items.title: Area levels
items.text:
Every biome has a fixed level. A creature's level is the level of the biome it stands in (stars don't change it): it sets the creature's accuracy and the item level of its loot, a chest takes the level of its biome, and gear bought from a trader the level of the biome the trader is in. It doesn't scale health or damage, except for the monolith bosses. With the Raid level scaling setting (off by default, on in Merciless), raiders take the level of the biome the raid comes from, and scale with it. Each biome also has a recommended player level: up to the next biome's, it gives full experience; past it, experience falls off.

Inside an arena with its own level (the dome of a rune monolith's boss, a map of the Halls of Oaths), creatures fight at that level and their loot takes it.

A creature in the Blight Mist takes the level of the next boss's biome by the world's progress (the first boss not yet defeated; the Deep North once Fader is), wherever it stands.

Biome Level Full experience up to level Meadows 1 19 Black Forest 19 43 Swamp 43 77 Mountain 77 97 Plains 97 130 Mistlands 130 181 Ashlands 181 246 Deep North 246 311

With the other mechanics: Experience and levels.

items.title: Experience fall-off
items.text:
Past a biome's recommended range, the combat experience you gain there fades. The ranges follow the recommended player levels (a server setting, by default the biomes' levels). The level that counts is yours; the biome is where the creature dies (for kills) or where you stand (for hits). Being below a biome's level costs nothing.

kept = max(0.05, 0.05 ^ (levels past the range ÷ 10))

Experience fades to 5% at 10 levels past the range, and never lower:

Levels past the range +1 +2 +3 +5 +8 +10 Experience kept 74.11% 54.93% 40.71% 22.36% 9.1% 5% Biome Full experience 5% from level Meadows 1–19 29 Black Forest 19–43 53 Swamp 43–77 87 Mountain 77–97 107 Plains 97–130 140 Mistlands 130–181 191 Ashlands 181–246 256 Deep North 246–311 321

items.title: Bleeding
items.text: Slash damage can inflict bleeding by chance; there is no base chance. Bleeding deals 20% of the slash damage of the hit that inflicted it per second for 4 s, over time and through armour. Each player keeps their own strongest bleed on a target; an equal or stronger one refreshes it.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
chance = flat chance × (1 + build-up) × more

Every hit with slash or poison damage rolls its chance to bleed or poison; how much damage the hit deals doesn't change the chance. There is no base chance: it comes from flat chance to bleed or poison and flat ailment chance, which build-up raises.

A hit bleeds at most once. For poison, every full 100% of chance applies one poison for certain and the rest is the chance of one more, each from the hit's poison damage.

With a stat that lets pierce damage bleed, 50% of the hit's pierce damage counts as slash for bleeding.

What it does: 20% of the slash damage per second for 4 s (80% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (physical). Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One bleed per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second.

Melee hits with Gravedigger's Needle bleed for 7 s at base instead.

Ailment damage multipliers for burning, poison and bleeding: × (1 + ailment damage increases, general and that ailment's) × their more multipliers; flat ailment damage adds its amount spread over 4 s. Each player's ailments tick on their own, once a second.

Damage over Time Speed: × (1 + its increases, general and that ailment's) × more, at least × 0.1. Burning, poison and bleeding deal their damage per second × that and end that much sooner, so the total stays the same.

items.text:
The strength with which a block pushes its attacker away. It is separate from block power, which absorbs damage.

Data from Path of Valheiman 6.0.12, extracted 2026-11-13.

items.title: Block
items.text: Block power absorbs part or all of an incoming hit; remaining damage passes through. Blocking spends stamina according to the strength of the hit.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Block: when you block a hit from the front, Valheim treats your block power like armour against the whole hit, every damage type, after the blocking item's own resistances.

block power = max(0, Valheim's block power × (1 + the shield's own block power increases) + flat block power) × (1 + block power increases) Valheim's block power = the item's block power at its quality × (1 + Blocking skill × 0.5) parry: block power × the item's parry bonus × (1 + parry bonus increases)

A parry is a block within 0.25 s of raising your guard, with an item that has a parry bonus. A block costs Valheim's block stamina × the share of your block power the hit used; a parry costs a fixed amount.

What gets through works like armour: block power under half the hit takes that much off; more than that cuts the hit to hit² ÷ (4 × block power). The rest goes on to your armour and rune shield.

If you're out of stamina, or the blocked hit's stagger breaks your guard, nothing is blocked. A hit that meets your block can't be a Glancing Blow.

Sigils in the blocking item's sockets add to its own block power and parry bonus increases. Stats that share part of your block power increases with parry bonus add that part to parry bonus increases.

items.title: Blunt damage
items.text: A physical damage type that builds armour break. Stagger uses the hit's separate stagger power.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
All the increased and reduced damage that applies to a hit is added into one sum, and the hit is multiplied by 1 + that sum once: general damage, your weapon kind's, melee, ranged or spell damage, attacks', alternative attacks', that of hits that aren't projectiles, a running attack's bonus, and the increases that depend on the enemy (below).

A scepter's hits count as the kind of attack they are: its spells take spell damage increases, its other attacks melee or ranged ones.

A sceptre's Smite also takes your area damage increases and flat area damage.

damage of a type = (weapon damage × skill multiplier + oils + flat damage × skill multiplier) × (1 + increases + that type's increases)

Each damage type adds its own increases to the sum, for that type only: fire, frost and lightning also add elemental damage increases, and slash, pierce and blunt add physical damage increases. So +50% damage and +50% fire damage make fire damage × 2, not × 2.25.

Projectiles: projectile damage increases join the sum too, with the projectile speed increases any of your stats turn into damage, and so do a torch's damage increases.

Bows and crossbows split each shot in two parts. The ammo's share is its damage ÷ (the weapon's damage + the ammo's), chopping and mining damage left out of both. That part takes the sum without your bow or crossbow damage increases, plus your projectile damage increases (bow or crossbow projectile ones included) and the increases of its damage type made for bow or crossbow shots (as a quiver's are); the weapon's part takes the sum as it is, without either.

damage = weapon's part × (1 + sum) + ammo's part × (1 + sum − bow or crossbow increases + projectile increases + the type's shot increases)

Chopping and mining: increases against trees, ore and resources join the same sum, and so flat damage against them grows with the whole sum.

Every step of a hit, in order: Order of a hit.

items.title: Boss
items.text: A biome's summoned boss. Defeating it can unlock progression; hanging its trophy at the Sacrificial Stones unlocks the corresponding Forsaken power.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
A boss summoned at its altar, or brought back with its place by a Great Rune of Awakening, can rise with stars: a 25% chance of at least one star, and 5% of two or more (part of the 25%). Past two, each further star has a 50% chance, up to the preset's most stars (5 on Normal), the same limit as for other creatures. By default, only once that boss has been defeated in the world. Runes of the Blood Challenge (up to 5) offered at a boss altar, Valheim's or that of one of the mod's bosses, give the next boss summoned there one star each instead of the roll, up to the preset's most stars, even before its first defeat or with boss stars turned off, with at least one modifier per star.

Health × 1.2 ^ stars Damage × 1.2 ^ stars

Modifiers per boss star: 0 on Normal, 1 on Hard and Merciless.

items.title: Build-up
items.text: Makes matching damage apply an ailment more readily. For burning and shock it enlarges each layer a hit leaves; for bleeding and poison it increases their chance, and its flat form is a flat chance. Chill and armour break still fill a gauge, impale uses an application chance.

items.title: Burning and shock: layers
items.text:
Flammability left by a hit = 20% × fire damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up) × more Conductivity left by a hit = 25% × lightning damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up) × more

Every fire hit leaves a layer of flammability on the enemy and every lightning hit a layer of conductivity, each for 8 s. The hit then ignites or shocks with a chance equal to all of that kind's layers on the enemy, its own included, at most 100%, plus your flat chance to ignite or shock × (1 + build-up) × more. Base health is the enemy's maximum health without the mod's difficulty scaling.

The layer one hit leaves, by its damage as a share of the enemy's base health:

Damage ÷ base health 5% 10% 25% 50% Flammability, +0% build-up 1.6% 3.2% 8% 16% Flammability, +100% build-up 3.2% 6.4% 16% 32% Conductivity, +0% build-up 2% 4% 10% 20% Conductivity, +100% build-up 4% 8% 20% 40%

A tarred enemy counts 30% more flammability (layers and tar together at most 100%); on a wet enemy each flammability layer is × 0.5.

Ground Effects that burn or shock add layers the same way and apply their ailment once the enemy's layers reach 50%.

items.title: Bleeding and poison: chance
items.text:
chance = flat chance × (1 + build-up) × more

Every hit with slash or poison damage rolls its chance to bleed or poison; how much damage the hit deals doesn't change the chance. There is no base chance: it comes from flat chance to bleed or poison and flat ailment chance, which build-up raises.

A hit bleeds at most once. For poison, every full 100% of chance applies one poison for certain and the rest is the chance of one more, each from the hit's poison damage.

With a stat that lets pierce damage bleed, 50% of the hit's pierce damage counts as slash for bleeding.

items.title: Chill: the gauge
items.text:
gauge filled by a hit = frost damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up)

How much of the gauge one hit fills, by its damage as a share of the enemy's base health:

Damage ÷ base health 5% 10% 25% 50% Filled, +0% build-up 8% 16% 40% 80% Filled, +100% build-up 16% 32% 80% 100%

At 100% chill starts, from the strongest frost hit since the gauge began to fill. The gauge then stays full, so every further frost hit applies chill again from its own damage. 3 s after the last frost hit the gauge drains, 25% per second; chill ends when it is empty (at most 7 s after that hit).

items.title: Patch history
items.text:
Patch Change Patch 6.0.0 Makes matching damage apply an ailment more readily. It → For does → burning not → and add → shock it enlarges each layer a missing → hit damage → leaves; type → for bleeding and poison it increases their chance, increase → and ailment → its damage → flat or → form extend → is duration; → a flat chance. Chill and armour break still fill a gauge, impale uses an application chance instead of a gauge.

Data from Path of Valheiman 6.0.12, extracted 2026-11-13.

items.title: Burning
items.text: Every fire hit leaves a layer of flammability on the target for 8 s, the larger the more of the target's ailment threshold it dealt; the layers add up to 100%, and each hit ignites with a chance equal to them. Burning deals 25% of the fire damage of the igniting hit per second for 4 s, over time; each player keeps their own strongest burn on a target. Tar makes a target more flammable, wet less and shortens burning; chill stops its damage while it lasts, and its time keeps running.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Flammability left by a hit = 20% × fire damage ÷ (62.5% × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up) × more

Every fire hit leaves a layer of flammability on the enemy and every lightning hit a layer of conductivity, each for 8 s. The hit then ignites or shocks with a chance equal to all of that kind's layers on the enemy, its own included, at most 100%, plus your flat chance to ignite or shock × (1 + build-up) × more. Base health is the enemy's maximum health without the mod's difficulty scaling.

A tarred enemy counts 30% more flammability (layers and tar together at most 100%); on a wet enemy each flammability layer is × 0.5.

Ground Effects that burn or shock add layers the same way and apply their ailment once the enemy's layers reach 50%.

What it does: 25% of the igniting hit's fire damage per second for 4 s (100% in all), × your ailment damage multipliers and damage over time multiplier (fire); fire damage increases don't apply again. Longer duration adds seconds, so more damage. One burn per player on an enemy: a new one replaces yours only if it deals at least as much per second. A wet enemy burns out 6 times as fast.

With Flame Without a Burial, your burning deals spirit damage instead of fire damage, × your damage over time multiplier for spirit.

Ailment damage multipliers for burning, poison and bleeding: × (1 + ailment damage increases, general and that ailment's) × their more multipliers; flat ailment damage adds its amount spread over 4 s. Each player's ailments tick on their own, once a second.

Damage over Time Speed: × (1 + its increases, general and that ailment's) × more, at least × 0.1. Burning, poison and bleeding deal their damage per second × that and end that much sooner, so the total stays the same.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Charged attack
items.text: A charge empowers your next released weapon attack and is consumed even on a miss. Charges do not stack or expire. A charge source can charge the attack again only after its cooldown: 2 s, a critical hit 1.2 s, counted from the last successful charge. A perfect dodge ignores the cooldown and always charges the attack if a dodge roll charges it for you. Spending a charge does not restart cooldowns, and failed grants do not extend them. All hits and projectiles of the released attack share its charge. Spells can consume it only with Charged Casts. The charge itself grants 25% increased damage; charged-attack nodes add further bonuses.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Charged attack: something charges your next weapon attack, and the next melee or ranged attack you release spends it, hit or miss (spells only with Charged Casts). One charge waits at a time; it doesn't stack or expire.

charged attack: + 25% increased damage, added to your other damage increases, and rows that work with charged attacks apply

A source charges again only 2 s after it last charged the attack (critical hits: 1.2 s). After any charge, every source also waits the shorter of its own cooldown and 3 s (cut by cooldown reduction and recovery). A perfect dodge ignores both cooldowns, but can't charge an attack that's already charged.

With Dash Punch, a charged fist or unarmed attack dashes to the target under your aim; one that isn't charged stays in place.

What charges the attack. Each source needs the passive or mastery option that grants it:

Charges the attack when Granted by an alternative attack hits an enemy Second edge you activate a trinket Flash Response you cast a spell Spell Primes the Strike you cover 25 m running on the ground or levitating, while no charge waits Giant's Run-Up you jump Leap Before the Blow you land a critical hit with an attack Critical Charge you parry a hit Ready Answer you start a dodge roll (a perfect dodge charges it even on cooldown) Rolling Charge

With Choose the Spend, only alternative attacks spend the charge; with Alternate Leads, alternative attacks don't spend it.

Unbound Charge: rolled once when the charge is spent. On success the attack gets 50% increased damage instead, and every row that works with charged attacks counts twice.

Hit splash: a charged attack's first hit on an enemy also hits every other enemy within 3 m × (1 + area of effect increases), for your splash share of its damage.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Damage conversion
items.text: Changes part of one damage type into another before percentage bonuses apply. Converted damage uses the ailments and resistances of its new type and the increases of both its new and its original type, and cannot be converted again; excessive conversion shares are reduced proportionally.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Damage conversion turns part of a hit's slash, pierce and blunt damage into another type, after flat damage and before increases; no other type converts. Each of the three converts by its own conversions plus those of all physical damage; if they come to more than 100%, they're scaled down to 100% together.

Conversion that depends on the enemy (against bosses, enemies with ailments and the like) counts too.

converted = slash, pierce or blunt × its conversion to the new type, all its conversions together at most 100%

Converted damage is its new type for resistances and ailments, but it grows with the increases of both types: its old type's and its new type's, added together.

Damage gained as extra: worked out from the slash, pierce and blunt damage before conversion, and added after it as its new type. It grows with its new type's increases only. Gain as extra of all damage is worked out from the hit's whole damage of every type instead. Gain as extra rolled on the weapon itself works the same way and also grows with the weapon's own increases of its new type.

Every step of a hit, in order: Order of a hit.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Armour break
items.text: Blunt hits progressively reduce the target's armour, including for the triggering hit. The reduction is shared on the target and clears after a pause without blunt hits.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Armour break: a hit's blunt damage breaks the enemy's armour the way it would fill an ailment gauge: blunt against its base health, raised by build-up. The broken share adds up to 100%, and everyone's hits on the enemy add to the same share; 8 s after the last hit that added to it (longer with armour break duration), it's gone.

broken share added by a hit = blunt ÷ (ailment threshold × the enemy's base health) × (1 + build-up) your physical damage + the enemy's armour × broken share × (1 + armour break effect increases), that share at most 100%

Every hit of yours on an enemy with broken armour gets that added, including the hit that just added to it, spread over its blunt, slash and pierce (as blunt if it has none). It comes before the enemy's armour, so it pays back about as much as the armour takes.

Curses that make the enemy take more armour break multiply the share each hit adds.

Build-up made for bow or crossbow shots (as a quiver's is) counts for bow and crossbow hits.

Melee hits with Victor's Right count × 0.5 of their blunt damage.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Critical hit
items.text: A critical hit multiplies the hit's damage. Increased critical chance scales the weapon's base chance; critical damage changes the multiplier separately.

items.title: Critical strike chance
items.text:
Critical strike chance starts from the weapon's base:

chance = (base + flat) × (1 + increases) × more, at most the maximum

Base: knives 15%, polearms 10%, other weapons 5%, spells 5%. The weapon's own critical chance properties apply to its base first. The maximum is 100% by default.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Critical strike damage
items.text:
Critical hits multiply the hit's damage by:

1.5 + critical damage bonuses, at least 0

The bonuses come in parts, each its flat bonuses × (1 + increases): general ones, those for your weapon kind, for the target, and for the alternative attack. The parts are computed separately and added up, so a general "reduced critical damage" doesn't lower your weapon's own bonus.

On a crossbow's last loaded shot (magazine), if you have critical damage increases for that shot, the multiplier is 1 + (0.5 + flat critical damage bonuses) × (1 + every critical damage increase that applies to the shot) × more critical damage: the increases then multiply the base too.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Crossbow fire rate
items.text: Crossbow fire rate sets the time between loaded shots. Each crossbow's base interval is a share of its own base reload time, so a 3.5 s reload gives about one shot per second. Reload speed changes only the reload.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Crossbows shoot from a magazine. Each crossbow reload (Valheim's reload, shortened by reload speed) fills it:

[loaded bolts](loaded-bolts.md) = ⌊(1 + flat loaded bolts + additional projectiles + ⌊additional projectile chance⌋, +1 with the chance of what is left) × (1 + loaded bolt increases) × more⌋, rolled when the reload finishes time between shots = the crossbow's reload time × 0.2857 ÷ ((1 + crossbow fire rate increases) × more)

Each shot fires one bolt and uses one loaded shot; a shot that saves its ammo keeps it. When the magazine is empty, the crossbow reloads; the Reload key (R by default) reloads early whenever the magazine isn't full. The first shot after a reload and the last loaded shot are magazine shots: bonuses can name them.

Critical damage increases for the last loaded shot change how its critical strike multiplier is built.
