items.title: Sockets
items.text: Up to three sockets hold sigils. Runic punches change the count by +1 (35%) or -1 (65%), within 0–3; Runecarver bonuses apply. Divine and corrupted punches recolour 1 to all ordinary sockets at random. No punch can be used with installed sigils. Divine sockets strengthen sigils by 50%. The count can fall to zero. A changed socket displays a floating +1 or −1.

items.title: Socket kinds
items.text:
Socket Takes Effect How it is made Ordinary (runic) Any sigil the item can take, except Sigils of Blight — Sockets on dropped items are ordinary. A Runic Punch adds one (35%) or removes the last (65%). Divine Any sigil the item can take, except Sigils of Blight The sigil in it is 50% stronger A Divine Punch turns from one to all of the ordinary sockets divine, at random. A socket a Runic Punch adds can come out divine with Runecarver bonuses for divine sockets. Corrupted Only Sigils of Blight: Sigil of the Oath Devourer, Sigil of the Crimson Brood — A Corrupted Punch turns from one to all of the ordinary sockets corrupted, at random. Phantom socket Any sigil the item can take, except Sigils of Blight — Added beyond the socket limit by runic crafting (see there).

Sigils of Blight ( Sigil of the Oath Devourer, Sigil of the Crimson Brood) fit only in corrupted sockets, and corrupted sockets take nothing else.

No punch can be used while a sigil sits in one of the item's sockets. A divine or corrupted punch needs at least one ordinary socket; it never changes the number of sockets. Rings, belts, trinkets, jewels and currency have no sockets.

An item has at most 3 sockets. Its corruption implicit can add one more, or make its sigils 25% stronger (on top of a divine socket).

items.title: Sockets on dropped items
items.text: A dropped item that can have sockets has them at 2% (magic), 4% (rare), 6% (unique) or 1% (otherwise). It then has one socket (85%), two (13%) or three (2%), all ordinary.

items.title: Intelligence
items.text: Per point: 0.185% increased eitr regeneration, +0.16 rune shield. Intelligence also contributes to the skill multiplier of the weapons it governs.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Each point of an attribute gives:

Attribute Per point Per 100 points Strength 0.125% increased health regeneration+0.2 carry weight 12.5% increased health regeneration+20 carry weight Dexterity 0.185% increased stamina regeneration0.2% increased evasion rating 18.5% increased stamina regeneration20% increased evasion rating Intelligence 0.185% increased eitr regeneration+0.16 rune shield 18.5% increased eitr regeneration+16 rune shield

Weapons governed by attributes multiply their damage by a random skill multiplier, picked anew for every hit between its midpoint − 0.15 and + 0.15, never below 0. The midpoint grows with the weapon's governing attribute points (with two, their average); Valheim's own weapon skill level doesn't count.

midpoint = 0.4 × (1 + 1.5 × (points ÷ 300)^0.75) Points 0 50 100 200 300 500 Midpoint 0.4 0.56 0.66 0.84 1 1.28

Governing attributes by weapon skill:

Weapon skill Governing attributes Swords Strength, Intelligence Knives Intelligence, Dexterity Clubs Strength Polearms Strength, Intelligence Spears Dexterity, Strength Axes Dexterity, Strength Bows Dexterity Elemental Magic Intelligence Blood Magic Intelligence Fists Dexterity Pickaxes Strength Crossbows Dexterity, Strength

Sceptres are governed by Strength and Intelligence, whatever their skill.

With Shifted Requirements, 50% of your Strength also counts as Dexterity for two-handed weapons and bows (not fist weapons).

items.title: Stagger power
items.text: The amount a hit contributes to the target's stagger gauge. A full gauge staggers the target; extra damage against staggered targets requires its own bonus.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Stagger fills from a hit's blunt, slash, pierce and lightning damage, as the target takes it. At its threshold, maximum health × the creature's own stagger factor, the target staggers. The gauge then drains: from full in 5 s for players, 25 s for enemies (the mod slows it).

Your own threshold counts 100% of your maximum rune shield as health, and your gauge drains that much faster, so it still empties in the same time.

your hit's stagger = (damage × 20% + flat) × (1 + stagger build-up) × the weapon's stagger multiplier

Your hits carry 20% of the stagger power Valheim gives them (a server setting); stagger build-up multiplies it and flat stagger build-up adds to it.

Forced stagger: when it rolls, the hit's stagger is multiplied by 100.

Stagger you take: × (1 − stagger resistance), which is at most 85%; cut by 50% while your rune shield holds. Stagger recovery drains your gauge faster.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Strike
items.text: A vertical melee weapon swing, primary or alternative. Horizontal swings and slams are not strikes, and a sceptre's strike is its Smite. Strike bonuses, strike copies and Critical Echo apply to these hits.

items.title: Additional strikes
items.text:
Strike: a melee weapon's vertical swing, primary or alternative (horizontal swings and thrusts don't count, whatever their animation); slams and sceptres don't count. Once a swing hits an enemy, it hits again as many times as your additional strikes, one every 0.12 s. Each goes to the nearest enemy not struck yet, within 5 m of the first target and 4.5 m of you; when there is none left, they stop.

additional strikes = ⌊additional strikes⌋, ×2 once after a critical strike (Double on Crit)

Each additional strike is a new hit of the same attack: it rolls its own critical strike and gets all your damage bonuses. Strike bonuses apply to the swing and to every additional strike.

With Double on Crit, the attack's first critical strike, from the swing or from one of its strikes, doubles its additional strikes, once per attack.

With All on One Target, every additional strike hits the first target instead, at 50% damage each, and they stop if it dies or gets out of reach.

Combo counts one hit per attack: additional strikes and phantom strikes never add to it.

With Echo Strikes for the weapon, its primary swing makes echo strikes in place of additional strikes.

A sceptre's strike is its Smite: it takes additional strikes as additional Smites.

Primary attacks that are strikes: Antler Pickaxe, Black Metal Pickaxe, Bronze Pickaxe, Iron Pickaxe, Stone Pickaxe.

Alternative attacks that are strikes: Black Metal Axe, Bloodgeon, Bronze Axe, Bronze Mace, Flametal Mace, Flint Axe, Frostfire Axe, Frostfire Mace, Frostner, Iron Axe, Iron Mace, Jotun Bane, Klossen, Nord Axe, Nord Mace, Porcupine, Stone Axe, Storm Star, Thunderblood Axe, Thunderblood Mace, Wooden Axe, Wooden Mace.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Smite
items.text:
Every swing of the Sceptre of the Pious (and of the uniques made from it: Bell Beneath the Mountain, Censer of the Forgotten Name) calls down Smite, a bolt of lightning. The swing itself hits like a club, with only the sceptre's physical damage; Smite carries its elemental damage (fire, frost, lightning, poison and spirit) at the sceptre's quality, and each swing costs 5 eitr. It lands on the first enemy the swing hit; if the swing hit none, on the nearest enemy within its radius of a point 2.5 m in front of you, or else on that point.

It hits every creature within 2.5 m × your area of effect of where it lands, except players and tamed creatures, × the sceptre's skill multiplier. Its hits can't be blocked or dodged. Each of them is a spell hit, a strike and an area hit at once (spells, strike): spell, strike and area damage bonuses all apply.

Additional Smites: your strike targets plus your additional strikes, whole ones only. Each lands on a different random enemy within 8 m × your area increases of the first, never on the first enemy again, and hits in the same way; with fewer enemies around, fewer land.

With All on One Target, they all strike the first enemy instead, at 50% damage each, and stop if it dies; with no enemy to land on, there are none.

With Double on Crit, a critical strike from one of a cast's Smites doubles its additional Smites, once per cast.

Casting Smite ends your combo.

Ground Effects: every Smite also leaves a spell ground patch where it lands.

A thrown Sceptre of the Pious, or a unique made from it, casts Smite where it lands, with the throw's damage.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Forced stagger
items.text: A successful roll forces the hit to stagger its target. This is separate from filling the stagger gauge; lightning hits can have an additional stagger chance.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Stagger fills from a hit's blunt, slash, pierce and lightning damage, as the target takes it. At its threshold, maximum health × the creature's own stagger factor, the target staggers. The gauge then drains: from full in 5 s for players, 25 s for enemies (the mod slows it).

Your own threshold counts 100% of your maximum rune shield as health, and your gauge drains that much faster, so it still empties in the same time.

your hit's stagger = (damage × 20% + flat) × (1 + stagger build-up) × the weapon's stagger multiplier

Your hits carry 20% of the stagger power Valheim gives them (a server setting); stagger build-up multiplies it and flat stagger build-up adds to it.

Forced stagger: when it rolls, the hit's stagger is multiplied by 100.

Stagger you take: × (1 − stagger resistance), which is at most 85%; cut by 50% while your rune shield holds. Stagger recovery drains your gauge faster.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Thorns
items.text: Automatically deals retaliatory pierce damage to an attacker. Added damage types can build their matching ailments.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Thorns: when a creature hits you and you don't evade it, it takes your thorns damage back. The amount doesn't depend on the hit: it's your flat thorns, or 5 if increased thorns are all you have.

thorns damage = flat thorns × (1 + damage increases + thorns increases + the damage type's increases) × block or parry multiplier × distance

It's pierce damage, unless your stats convert part of it to other types or add more as extra damage.

Full damage to an attacker within 3 m of you (from its edge), falling to nothing at 8 m.

On a shield block with Spiked Shield: × 150%. Thorns that work with parries add to a parry's thorns.

Thorns increases and more multipliers that apply only against certain enemies (bosses, burning enemies and the like) count for the attacker and multiply on top, as their own factor.

Thorny Carapace also deals your thorns to enemies touching you, once every 1 s per enemy, shorter with cooldown reduction and recovery.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Experience
items.text: Character experience comes from combat only and advances the main passive tree; peaceful work gives craft experience to the crafting tree instead. Death can remove current-level character experience without removing allocated points.

items.title: Experience
items.text:
Only combat raises your character level: kills, and the hits of your fighting skills. Everything peaceful (gathering, building, crafting, exploring, travelling) goes to craft experience instead, and the experience fall-off never cuts it.

Experience from a kill:

Experience = base health × 0.4 × (1 + 0.5 × stars + 0.5 × modifiers)

Base health is the Valheim health of its kind. It is shared between the players alive within 40 m (2.5× that for bosses). At night, every experience gain is +50%. Creatures of a runic event give 10%.

With the other mechanics: Experience and levels.

items.title: Experience fall-off
items.text:
Past a biome's recommended range, the combat experience you gain there fades. The ranges follow the recommended player levels (a server setting, by default the biomes' levels). The level that counts is yours; the biome is where the creature dies (for kills) or where you stand (for hits). Being below a biome's level costs nothing.

kept = max(0.05, 0.05 ^ (levels past the range ÷ 10))

Experience fades to 5% at 10 levels past the range, and never lower:

Levels past the range +1 +2 +3 +5 +8 +10 Experience kept 74.11% 54.93% 40.71% 22.36% 9.1% 5% Biome Full experience 5% from level Meadows 1–19 29 Black Forest 19–43 53 Swamp 43–77 87 Mountain 77–97 107 Plains 97–130 140 Mistlands 130–181 191 Ashlands 181–246 256 Deep North 246–311 321

With the other mechanics: Experience and levels.

items.title: Character level
items.text:
Combat experience raises your character level, up to 200. Each level needs:

experience to the next level = 20.7 × level ^ 1.1, rounded Level To the next level Total to reach 2 44 21 10 261 1,112 25 714 8,143 50 1,531 35,676 75 2,391 84,192 100 3,281 154,589 125 4,193 247,519 150 5,125 363,494 175 6,072 502,944 200 — 666,239

Each level gives 1 passive point; points also come from other sources.

On death you lose 10% of a level's experience (experience lost on death), never going below the start of your level. Passives can lower the loss.

items.title: Halls of Oaths
items.text: The Halls of Oaths are dungeons you plan yourself. At a gate of the halls you lay room items on the board of the Book of the Halls, pack them into a map, enchant it with runes for map modifiers and launch it. The dungeon is built exactly as planned, and its final boss gives a pair of ascension points.

items.title: Gates and lobbies
items.text:
Gates of the Halls of Oaths stand in the world. A gate's level is the level of the land around it: it sets the size of the board, the level of the enemies and the tier of the map. Use a gate to enter its lobby, or hold the alternative key (Shift) while using it for a lobby of your own.

A lobby with the book of the halls: build a map from room items and launch it

The lobby is a safe hall in the style of the gate's biome. It holds the Book of the Halls, the room merchant Hallvard Stone-Tally and the great door into the dungeon.

Hugin waits above the book with 5 hints:

  • Rooms: The halls are built from rooms. Rooms drop from enemies, elites, dungeons and bosses, and the room merchant in the lobby sells them.
  • The board: Lay rooms from your bag on the book's board: a stack is taken whole, each click lays one. A path must lead from the entrance to the top row. Into the top cell goes a boss room: whichever biome, that boss.
  • Map and runes: Pack the board into a map. Runes give the map properties: danger and reward.
  • Ascension: Ascension and the tier's points come only from the boss of the top cell. The tier follows the halls: the Black Forest and the Swamp are the first, the Mountains and the Plains the second, the Mistlands the third, the Ashlands the fourth.
  • Boss rooms: The rooms of the biomes' bosses drop once that boss has been defeated in this world. Brenna, Geirrhafa, Zil and Thungr and Lord Reto are the halls' own bosses: their rooms drop in their lands from the start.

items.title: The Book of the Halls
items.text:
The book lays a board of cells. The entrance is in the bottom row, and the final boss's cell is the only cell of the top row; the other cells are open or closed at random, and every board can be walked from the entrance to the cell under the boss. The number of open cells grows with the gate's level:

open cells = 5 at gate level 19 or lower, rising evenly to 30 at level 181; the board is as wide as √(cells ÷ 0.55), rounded Gate in Level Open cells Board (width × height) Shortest way at least Meadows 1 5 3 × 5 3 Black Forest 19 5 3 × 5 3 Swamp 43 9 4 × 6 4 Mountains 77 14 5 × 7 4 Plains 97 17 6 × 7 4 Mistlands 130 22 6 × 8 4 Ashlands 181 30 7 × 8 4 Deep North 246 30 7 × 8 4

A map holds at most 24 rooms, its boss room included. The top cell takes only a boss room, of any biome, and a map can't be packed without one. Every room must connect to the entrance, and the shortest way from the entrance to the boss must be at least as long as shown.

Rooms go on open cells from your own bag: pick up a room and click a cell (a stack is taken whole, each click lays one). Right-click takes a room back to the bag, and dropping another room on it replaces it. Neighbouring rooms join by themselves: Dead end, Corridor, Corner, T-junction, Crossroads. When a room can't go on a cell or the board has a problem, the book says why. A new board returns the rooms on the old one to the bag.

Packing turns the placed rooms into a map in the book's cell: the rooms are spent, the plan no longer changes, and the map stays in its cell (it can't be taken out, moved or given away). Until it is launched, a packed map can be enchanted with runes for map modifiers.

items.title: Launching
items.text: The map is launched from the book. Every player within 30 m of whoever launches it goes in as one party: the great door rises and the party walks into the dungeon. The dungeon is built exactly as the rooms lie on the board, each room in the architecture and atmosphere of its biome, with enemies of its biome scaled to the gate's level. While the halls are open the map can't be changed; a new map can be launched once the last player is out and the door has come down.

items.title: Sealed fights
items.text:
A fight room seals while its fight lasts and opens once it is cleared. Party members can always join a sealed room, and the fight grows for each one who comes in.

For one player a room holds 28 enemies in all, reinforcements included, with up to 18 alive at once, plus 2 elites. Each more player in the room adds 50% to both counts, one more elite for every 2 more players, and 30% health to every enemy (70% to bosses). A room never has more than 32 enemies alive at once.

Elites have 1 star, with a 35% chance of one more. The final boss has 2 more stars, plus those of Crowned Guardian; Rising Host adds its stars to every enemy.

items.title: The final boss
items.text: The boss room in the top cell sets the final boss: the boss of its biome at full size, in a tall arena of its biome at the top of the map. After the fight the ascension altar wakes in the arena and a portal leads back to the lobby. Boss rooms on other cells are extra boss fights with their own loot (see boss rooms).

items.title: Deaths
items.text: A player who falls in the halls respawns in their lobby, not at their bed, and their grave lies in the lobby; these halls stay closed to them for good. The run fails when every member of the party has fallen. With a single life, a death in the halls is not a real death: the character is not lost.

items.title: Ascension points
items.text:
A map's final boss gives a pair of ascension points (2) for the map's tier, once per character for each tier: 8 points from the four tiers in all. A map's tier is its gate's tier, by the gate's level; gates below the first tier give none. The points are taken at the ascension altar, where you also choose your class: see Ascendancy. Under the launch button the book shows whether the map will give you points.

Tier Gate level Gates in Ascension points Training path < 19 Meadows — I · Oath of the Hearth 19+ Black Forest, Swamp +2 II · Oath of Stone 77+ Mountains, Plains +2 III · Oath of Mist 130+ Mistlands +2 IV · Oath of Ash 181+ Ashlands, Deep North +2

Only those who stood to the end take the pair: the party members still alive when the boss falls, and those who fell in the boss's own arena.

items.title: The room merchant
items.text:
Hallvard Stone-Tally stands in the lobby and sells room items: 8 offers, drawn with the rooms' drop weights from the ordinary and boss rooms the gate's level reaches (a biome boss's room only once that boss has fallen in the world). Unique rooms are never for sale. His stock renews every 3 in-game days.

A Rune of Renewed Trade renews his stock at once: right-click it in the bag while his shop is open.

items.title: Map modifiers
items.text:
A map packed in the Book of the Halls can be enchanted with runes for modifiers. Each modifier gives a reward, most of them with a danger attached. Higher-level maps roll stronger modifiers.

Use runes to enchant the halls with modifiers and increase rewards

items.title: Grades and runes
items.text:
A map's grade follows the number of its modifiers; a map holds at most 6. A modifier family appears only once on a map, and some modifiers need a room type or a boss on the map.

Grade Modifiers Normal map 0 Magic map 1–2 Rare map 3–6

items.title: Runes on a map
items.text:
Runes are applied as on items: right-click the rune in the bag, then click the map in the book. They act only on a packed map before it is launched. A rune that can't act on the map, and any other rune, is refused and not spent.

Rune On a map Rune of Spark Adds the first modifier to a normal map. Rune of Weaving Adds a second modifier to a magic map with one. Rune of Change Rerolls a magic map's modifiers into one or two new ones. Great Rune of the Jarl Adds a modifier to a magic map. Great Rune of Ascent Adds a modifier to a rare map, up to 6. Great Rune of Oblivion Removes one random modifier. Great Rune of Fate Rerolls the numbers of every modifier within its tier.

items.title: How a modifier rolls
items.text:
A new modifier is picked by weight among those that fit the map. Its tier is then picked among the tiers the map's level reaches, by the tier weights below, and it gets a roll from 0 to 1: its numbers lie between the next tier's and its own tier's, by the roll (for the lowest tier, between 80% of its numbers and its numbers). Counts such as item racks or rune mines are rounded to whole numbers; stars and bosses take their tier's number.

items.title: Room items
items.text:
Room items are the rooms you lay on the board of the Book of the Halls. Any room goes on any map: its biome decides where it drops, the architecture it is built in and the enemies that hold it. Ordinary and boss rooms stack up to 20; unique rooms don't stack.

Place it on the board of the Book of the Halls, by a gate of the halls

items.title: Where rooms drop
items.text:
Room items drop like currency from creatures and chests: their family competes with the other currency families by the total weight of the rooms that can drop at that spot, and the rarer the drop, the more it favours boss and unique rooms. A room drops only where its row allows it: in its biome, from a land level on, from elite enemies and bosses, or once a biome's boss has fallen in the world. Creatures inside the halls never drop room items.

On top of that, every kill and chest outside the halls rolls extra room items: on average 7 × as many as its currency drops give rooms, picked by the rooms' weights alone (not by rarity). Rooms so drop about 8 times as often as their share of the currency gives.

items.title: Enchantments
items.text: Enchantments are properties you choose and put on an item yourself, at the Runecarver Table. You open them by reading scrolls. Each enchantment has five tiers, from T5 (the weakest) to T1, and some also have a special T0.

items.title: How enchanting works
items.text:
• Enchanting is done in the Enchant tab of the Rune Carver Table. Only the tiers your character has opened with scrolls can be used. What a character learns stays with that character.
  • An item holds one enchantment. It takes a free prefix or suffix place, as many as the item's rarity allows. A plain item counts as magic for this and becomes magic once enchanted. It can't be a kind of property the item already has. The tooltip shows it lighter than ordinary properties.
  • Any opened tier goes on an item of any level: the opened tier is the only requirement.
  • Unique items, special jewels, unidentified items and corrupted items can't be enchanted.
  • The value rolls within the tier's range. Like any item mod, a property that scales with the item slot is multiplied by the slot multiplier.
  • The table's remove button takes 10 Azurite Dust and removes the enchantment together with its property. Anything else that takes the property away removes the enchantment too: forging at the Runic Anvil (unless the property is kept) and the glyphs that remove properties (Unbinding Glyph of Prefixes, Unbinding Glyph of Suffixes, Glyph of Cleansing, Sifting Glyph).
  • Rune of the Crimson Seal seals one random property of a rare item that has a full set of properties and no influence. If it seals the enchanted property, that property stays on as an ordinary sealed property and the item counts as unenchanted. A new enchantment can then go on once a prefix or suffix place is free.

items.title: Cost
items.text:
Each tier has its own cost, taken from your bag when you enchant:

Tier Azurite Dust Divine Azurite Dust T0 250 60 T1 160 25 T2 110 10 T3 70 — T4 40 — T5 20 —

Removing an enchantment costs 10 Azurite Dust.

items.title: Enchantments by item kind
items.text:
The Enchant tab lists the enchantments for each kind of item. An item placed on the table opens the list for its own kind. The values are each tier's range as the tab shows it, and the T0 column names the special tier.

items.text:

items.title: Skill gems
items.text: Skill gems go on the skill board in the equipment window (tab Skills). Each one's text is the game's own; a number shown as a range changes from rank 1 to rank 5. Capacity is how much of the board's capacity it takes, price what it costs while it works.

items.title: Triggers (6)
items.text:
React to an event and start the effects beside them. Each effect they start raises the stamina cost of every attack or block.

Name Effect Capacity Price Cut from On Hit When an attack hits an enemy: 25–35% chance to trigger the connected effects. Once per attack, at most every 0.6 s. 2 Attack stamina cost: +6% per effect Uncut Trigger Gem On Critical Hit When an attack hits an enemy critically: 50–70% chance to trigger the connected effects. Once per attack, at most every 0.4 s. 2 Attack stamina cost: +6% per effect Uncut Trigger Gem On Block When a block stops a hit: triggers the connected effects. At most every 1–0.6 s. 2 Block stamina cost: +8% per effect Uncut Trigger Gem On Parry When a parry stops a hit: triggers the connected effects. An ordinary block does not. At most every 0.5–0.3 s. 2 Block stamina cost: +8% per effect Uncut Trigger Gem On Killing a Burning Enemy When an attack kills a burning enemy: 35–49% chance to trigger the connected effects at the corpse. 2 Attack stamina cost: +4% per effect Uncut Trigger GemAfter Fader is defeated On Killing a Bleeding Enemy When an attack kills a bleeding enemy: 35–49% chance to trigger the connected effects at the corpse. 2 Attack stamina cost: +4% per effect Uncut Trigger GemAfter The Queen is defeated

items.title: Effects (11)
items.text:
Do something when a trigger beside them fires.

Name Effect Capacity Price Cut from Eikthyr's Spark Chain lightning strikes up to 3 enemies, each for 50–70% of the weapon's base damage as lightning damage. 3 — Uncut Effect GemAfter Eikthyr is defeated Night Brood Summons 2 bats that fight for 12 s. Up to 4 bats live at once; the brood rests 8 s between summons. 3 — Uncut Effect GemAfter Moder is defeated Frost Wave A wave of cold around the bearer: 40–56% of the weapon's base damage as frost damage to enemies within 5 m. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Victor's Blood Heals the bearer for 8–11.2% of maximum health. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Shard of Retribution Returns 40–56% of the stopped hit's damage to the attacker, as the same kinds of damage. Only from an incoming hit. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Bowstring Echo Looses a spectral echo of the triggering shot at the struck enemy for 50–70% of its damage. The echo leaves no ammunition and does not echo again. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Ice Shards 3 ice shards burst from the target at the nearest other enemies within 10 m, each dealing 35–49% of the weapon's base damage as frost damage. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Fire Burst A burst of fire at the target: 50–70% of the weapon's base damage as fire damage to enemies within 2.5 m. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Flame of the Fallen The corpse explodes for 6–8.4% of its maximum health as fire damage to enemies within 5 m. Bosses explode for 25% of that. 3 — Uncut Effect GemAfter Fader is defeated Blood Legacy The corpse bursts: 50–70% of its remaining bleeding damage strikes enemies within 5 m as physical damage. No bleed left, no burst. 3 — Uncut Effect GemAfter The Queen is defeated Flesh Rend Deals extra damage equal to 2–2.8% of the target's maximum health, as the kinds of damage of the triggering hit. Bosses take 20% of it. 3 — Uncut Effect GemAfter Yagluth is defeated

items.title: Curses (8)
items.text:
Effects that curse the target. One player keeps one curse on each enemy.

Name Effect Capacity Price Cut from Broken Seals Curses the target: -(15–21)% fire, frost and lightning resistance for 6 s. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Rotten Blood Curses the target: -(20–28)% poison resistance for 6 s. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Bared Soul Curses the target: -(20–28)% spirit resistance for 6 s. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Broken Will Curses the target: it deals 20–28% less damage for 6 s. Bosses: 50% of the effect. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Norns' Fetters Curses the target: 20–28% less movement and attack speed for 6 s. Bosses: 50% of the effect. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Bared Steel Curses the target: 25–35% less armour against hits for 6 s. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Trembling Bones Curses the target: it takes 30–42% more stagger build-up for 6 s. Does not stagger by itself. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem Shattered Mail Curses the target: it takes 30–42% more armour break build-up for 6 s. 3 — Uncut Effect Gem

items.title: Supports (14)
items.text:
Change the effects and auras beside them, with a drawback. They take capacity for each gem they support.

items.title: Divine Azurite
items.text:
Materials

A golden radiance runs through the stone, as if a god had touched it.

items.title: Mining
items.text:
Starts appearing in the Swamp: the first time you come within 30 m of a plain azurite vein, a heavenly strike can turn it divine. Chance by biome: Swamp, Mountain: 5%; Plains, Mistlands, Ashlands, Deep North: 10%. In the Plains, Mistlands, Ashlands, Deep North it is certain after 9 misses in a row. Not inside a Blight Mist.

The craft mastery Divine Touch can also turn a plain vein divine while you cut it.

Needs a rune chisel of this tier or higher: Bronze Rune Chisel / Iron Rune Chisel / Black Metal Rune Chisel / Flametal Rune Chisel. Pickaxes can't cut azurite veins.

These veins are ×2.5 as hard to cut as plain ones.

items.title: Enchantment scrolls
items.text: Three kinds of scroll open enchantments. They are kept in the bag as currency. Right-click to learn: the scroll teaches its enchantments to the character that reads it and is used up. A scroll whose enchantments the character already knows is not spent. See all enchantments.

items.title: Scroll of Enchantment
items.text:
Opens the enchantments of its theme. The scroll's stage (I to V) sets the highest tier it opens. Reading a higher stage also opens the tiers in between; a scroll of a stage you already have, or lower, teaches nothing.

Stage Opens I Opens these enchantments from T5 to T5 II Opens these enchantments from T5 to T4 III Opens these enchantments from T5 to T3 IV Opens these enchantments from T5 to T2 V Opens these enchantments from T5 to T1

items.title: Where theme scrolls drop
items.text:
Each loot drop from these sources has a chance to add a Scroll of Enchantment (when the server lets that source drop currency):

Source Chance Boss 60% Elite creature with 2 or more stars 8% Elite creature with 1 star 4% Dungeon chest 12% Chest 3%

The scroll's stage follows the level of what it drops from: the stage of the biome that level belongs to. A boss without a level of its own counts by its biome, and the ocean counts as stage II.

Stage Biomes I Meadows, Black Forest II Swamp III Mountain IV Plains V Mistlands, Ashlands, Deep North

The theme is picked at random among the themes that have enchantments and that the character hasn't yet opened up to that stage. When every theme is, no scroll drops: what you already know never drops.

items.title: Scroll of Exalted Enchantment
items.text:
Opens the special T0 of this enchantment.

A boss above level 130 (the Mistlands' level; see creature level), in the world or in the halls, gives each living player within 60 m a chance of 8% at an exalted scroll of their own. It opens the T0 of a random enchantment that player doesn't know yet.

items.title: Cuts into
items.text:
Name Effect Eikthyr's Spark Chain lightning strikes up to 3 enemies, each for 50–70% of the weapon's base damage as lightning damage. After Eikthyr is defeated Night Brood Summons 2 bats that fight for 12 s. Up to 4 bats live at once; the brood rests 8 s between summons. After Moder is defeated Frost Wave A wave of cold around the bearer: 40–56% of the weapon's base damage as frost damage to enemies within 5 m. Victor's Blood Heals the bearer for 8–11.2% of maximum health. Shard of Retribution Returns 40–56% of the stopped hit's damage to the attacker, as the same kinds of damage. Only from an incoming hit. Bowstring Echo Looses a spectral echo of the triggering shot at the struck enemy for 50–70% of its damage. The echo leaves no ammunition and does not echo again. Ice Shards 3 ice shards burst from the target at the nearest other enemies within 10 m, each dealing 35–49% of the weapon's base damage as frost damage. Fire Burst A burst of fire at the target: 50–70% of the weapon's base damage as fire damage to enemies within 2.5 m. Flame of the Fallen The corpse explodes for 6–8.4% of its maximum health as fire damage to enemies within 5 m. Bosses explode for 25% of that. After Fader is defeated Blood Legacy The corpse bursts: 50–70% of its remaining bleeding damage strikes enemies within 5 m as physical damage. No bleed left, no burst. After The Queen is defeated Flesh Rend Deals extra damage equal to 2–2.8% of the target's maximum health, as the kinds of damage of the triggering hit. Bosses take 20% of it. After Yagluth is defeated Broken Seals Curses the target: -(15–21)% fire, frost and lightning resistance for 6 s. Rotten Blood Curses the target: -(20–28)% poison resistance for 6 s. Bared Soul Curses the target: -(20–28)% spirit resistance for 6 s. Broken Will Curses the target: it deals 20–28% less damage for 6 s. Bosses: 50% of the effect. Norns' Fetters Curses the target: 20–28% less movement and attack speed for 6 s. Bosses: 50% of the effect. Bared Steel Curses the target: 25–35% less armour against hits for 6 s. Trembling Bones Curses the target: it takes 30–42% more stagger build-up for 6 s. Does not stagger by itself. Shattered Mail Curses the target: it takes 30–42% more armour break build-up for 6 s. Rune Veil The bearer and allies within 8 m have +30–42 maximum rune shield. Entering the aura raises the maximum, it does not fill it. Plague Breath Enemies within 6 m take 6–8.4 poison damage per second. The bearer breathes it too: 15–12% of it per second. Warm Hearth The bearer and allies within 8 m regenerate 2–2.8 health per second. Steadfast Circle The bearer and allies within 8 m have 30–42% increased endurance. Circle of Gifts Turns the supports next to it into their aura forms and grants them, with their drawbacks, to the bearer and allies within 8 m. Takes no effects or curses. Storm Crown While the bearer is airborne, every 1.2 s a bolt strikes a random enemy within 30 m for 40–56% of the weapon's base damage as lightning damage. On the ground the crown is quiet; its eitr stays reserved. After Eikthyr is defeated Answering Heat Incoming fire feeds a burning ring: for 1 s enemies within 4 m take 50–70% of the fire damage incoming in the last second, per second. Incoming fire is counted before any reduction. No incoming fire, no damage. After Yagluth is defeated Rain Underfoot A rain cloud follows the bearer: everything within 3–4.2 m beneath it gets wet, as in rain. No levitation, no damage. After The Queen is defeated Circle of Malice Keeps the curses next to it on enemies within 8–11.2 m while they stay inside. Every curse counts against the curse limit on each enemy.

items.title: Skill board
items.text:
The skill board holds the skill gems in the equipment window, tab Skills. Gems work through the cells they share a side with.

Put a gem from the bag on an open cell: pick it up and click the cell, or right-click it in the bag. Gems work through the cells they share a side with: a trigger starts the effects next to it, supports change their neighbours, auras work by themselves once switched on. Drag gems between cells to swap them; right-click a gem to take it back.

items.title: Cells
items.text:
The board has 19 hexagonal cells in two rings around the centre; 4 are open from the start (filled above). Each Awakening Chisel opens one more locked cell.

A Awakening Chisel opens it: right-click the chisel in the bag, then left-click this cell. An open cell adds no capacity.

items.title: How gems connect
items.text:
• Trigger: A gem that reacts to an event - a hit, a critical hit, a block, a parry, a kill - and starts every compatible effect next to it at once. Its effects make the attack or block that pays for them cost more stamina, whether the event happens or not.
  • Effect: A gem that does something when a trigger next to it starts it: a bolt, a wave, a heal, a curse. With two triggers beside it, it takes one of them; the board window switches which.
  • Curse: A debuff on an enemy: lower resistance, weaker blows, slower actions or more build-up taken. One player keeps one curse on each enemy; a repeated curse refreshes itself, a new one replaces the oldest.
  • Support: A gem that changes the effects and auras next to it, with its drawback. It never changes triggers or other supports, and it reaches nothing beyond its neighbours.
  • Aura: A gem that works by itself while switched on and reserves eitr. Supports next to it change it; the Circle of Gifts grants the aura forms of its supports, the Circle of Malice keeps its curses on enemies inside.

An effect takes one trigger beside it that can start it: the one chosen in the board window, or else the first in board order. A curse can take a Circle of Malice beside it instead. A trigger works only when it starts at least one effect; when it fires, it starts all of them. A support changes every effect or aura beside it whose tags it supports (listed on its page); the Circle of Gifts takes every support beside it. Auras need no trigger: they work while switched on.

items.title: Which trigger starts which effect
items.text:
A trigger gives its effects what its event has: a living target, a shot, an incoming hit, a corpse. An effect that needs more than that stays unconnected.

Effect On Hit On Critical Hit On Block On Parry On Killing a Burning Enemy On Killing a Bleeding Enemy Eikthyr's Spark ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Night Brood ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Frost Wave ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Victor's Blood ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Shard of Retribution — — ✓ ✓ — — Bowstring Echo ✓ ✓ — — — — Ice Shards ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Fire Burst ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Flame of the Fallen — — — — ✓ — Blood Legacy — — — — — ✓ Flesh Rend ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ — — Broken Seals ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ — — Rotten Blood ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ — — Bared Soul ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ — — Broken Will ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ — — Norns' Fetters ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ — — Bared Steel ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ — — Trembling Bones ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ — — Shattered Mail ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ — —

✓: the trigger starts the effect; —: it cannot (hover for the game's reason). On Block also fires on parries.

items.title: States
items.text:
A gem's tooltip on the board says what it is doing:

  • Working: connected and working.
  • Not connected: nothing beside it to work with.
  • Incompatible: only triggers that cannot start it are beside it.
  • Switched off: an aura that is switched off; left-click switches it on.
  • Waiting for eitr: an aura that does not fit in what is left of maximum eitr.
  • Over capacity: the board takes more capacity than it has: nothing on it works.

items.title: Capacity
items.text:
capacity = 8 + min(12, ⌊passive points earned ÷ 10⌋)

Every gem on the board takes capacity, connected or not. A new character has 8; every 10 passive points earned add one, up to 20 at 120 points. Opening a cell adds none.

Gem Capacity Trigger 2 Effect 3 Curse 3 Support 1 per supported gem Aura 3 Aura: Circle of Gifts, Circle of Malice 4

Over capacity: the board does not work until gems leave it or capacity grows. Placing a gem that would take more capacity than the board has is refused.

items.title: Stamina cost
items.text:
Hit, critical hit and kill triggers raise the stamina cost of every attack, hit or miss; block and parry triggers raise the stamina cost of every block, once per block. It is paid whether the trigger fires or not.

cost added by a trigger = Σ over its working effects (its price per effect + 3% × supports of that effect) × the effect's cost multiplier

The cost multiplier comes from the effect's supports: Long Seal makes it cost more, Thrifty Facet less; Long Seal's longer duration also adds half of itself on effects with the Duration tag. The attack's or block's stamina is multiplied by 1 + the sum of its triggers' costs.

Example: On Hit beside Eikthyr's Spark with two supports adds 6% + 2 × 3% = 12% to every attack's stamina.

Name Price On Hit Each effect it starts: +6% attack stamina cost, paid on every attack, hit or miss On Critical Hit Each effect it starts: +6% attack stamina cost, paid on every attack, hit or miss On Block Each effect it starts: +8% block stamina cost, paid on every block On Parry Each effect it starts: +8% block stamina cost, paid on every block On Killing a Burning Enemy Each effect it starts: +4% attack stamina cost, paid on every attack, hit or miss On Killing a Bleeding Enemy Each effect it starts: +4% attack stamina cost, paid on every attack, hit or miss

items.title: Eitr reserve
items.text:
A switched-on aura keeps part of maximum eitr for itself while it works; each support of the aura reserves more. If maximum eitr falls, the last auras in board order wait until it fits again.

reserve = (the aura's share × maximum eitr + 5 × supports beside it) × its supports' cost multiplier × (1 − reservation efficiency)

The share is of the whole maximum eitr. Auras reserve in board order out of what is left once your summons and bells hold theirs (held eitr): one that does not fit waits (Waiting for eitr) and the next one is still tried; with 1 maximum eitr or less, none fits. A switched-off aura, or a board over capacity, reserves nothing. Switching on or placing a gem that would leave an aura waiting is refused. Reservation efficiency counts up to 75%.

The Circle of Gifts adds its own amount per support instead; the Circle of Malice also adds 10 per curse it keeps, and 3–2.4 more for each Heavy Word on a kept curse.

Example: Warm Hearth (25%) with one support, at 200 maximum eitr, reserves 25% × 200 + 5 = 55 eitr.

Name Price Each one beside it Rune Veil 25% +5 per support Plague Breath 25% +5 per support Warm Hearth 25% +5 per support Steadfast Circle 50% +5 per support Circle of Gifts 50% +6 per support Storm Crown 15% +5 per support Answering Heat 15% +5 per support Rain Underfoot 15% +5 per support Circle of Malice 50% +5 per support+10 per curse kept

items.title: Auras at work
items.text:
aura strength = (1 + increased aura effect) × more aura effect × (1 + its supports' effect) × (1 + 10% × (rank − 1))

The strength multiplies the aura's own numbers (rune shield, regeneration, endurance, poison damage) and what the Circle of Gifts grants. Inner Circle adds to its supports' effect; Wide Echo takes from the effect of an aura that deals no damage.

An aura supported by Inner Circle affects only its bearer: allies around it gain nothing.

The Circle of Gifts grants each support beside it as an aura form (aura forms): its increases × the circle's strength × (1 + 10% × (support rank − 1)); its overflowing chances follow the support's rank alone, and its drawbacks soften with that rank.

Plague Breath and Answering Heat deal damage over time instead of hits. Every 0.5 s, Plague Breath deals 0.5 s of its poison damage per second to each enemy in range. Fire damage taken lights Answering Heat: for its duration, every 0.25 s it deals 0.25 s of its share of the fire taken in the last second. These ticks cannot be blocked or dodged, and neither stagger nor push; the character's increased and more damage count, with its damage for area, damage over time and auras (and spells, for a Spell gem).

items.title: Gems and your stats
items.text: A gem effect counts the character's own stats for what it is: increased damage and the damage of its kind (area, projectile, spell for a Spell gem), area of effect, effect duration, extra projectiles, pierce and chains, shot speed and knockback. Its supports' numbers (an overflowing chance, increased area, longer duration) add into the same sums as the character's own, and its hits then go through the character's hit rules like any other hit.

items.title: Curses
items.text:
A debuff on an enemy: lower resistance, weaker blows, slower actions or more build-up taken. One player keeps one curse on each enemy; a repeated curse refreshes itself, a new one replaces the oldest.

One player keeps 1 curse on each enemy; Double Malice raises that (at most 8). Other players' curses do not count against yours.

A curse you already keep on the enemy refreshes: it lasts until the later end and keeps the stronger value. A new one past your limit replaces your oldest; a curse kept by the Circle of Malice is refused instead.

curse value = its value at its rank × (1 + increased curse effect + [Heavy Word](support-curse-power.md)), at most 75%

Passives that increase curse effect include Weight of Words.

duration = 6 s × (1 + increased curse and effect duration) × more effect duration × [Long Seal](duration.md) × [Heavy Word](support-curse-power.md), at most 120 s

Passives that increase curse duration include Weight of Words.

Name Effect Broken Seals Curses the target: -(15–21)% fire, frost and lightning resistance for 6 s. Rotten Blood Curses the target: -(20–28)% poison resistance for 6 s. Bared Soul Curses the target: -(20–28)% spirit resistance for 6 s. Broken Will Curses the target: it deals 20–28% less damage for 6 s. Bosses: 50% of the effect. Norns' Fetters Curses the target: 20–28% less movement and attack speed for 6 s. Bosses: 50% of the effect. Bared Steel Curses the target: 25–35% less armour against hits for 6 s. Trembling Bones Curses the target: it takes 30–42% more stagger build-up for 6 s. Does not stagger by itself. Shattered Mail Curses the target: it takes 30–42% more armour break build-up for 6 s.

items.title: Ranks and cutting
items.text:
A gem has a rank from 1 to 5. Every rank above 1 changes something:

  • What the gem does (damage shares, heals, curse values, support bonuses, an aura's whole effect) grows by 10% of its rank-1 value.
  • A drawback (a support's less damage, longer rest or higher cost; what an aura does to its own bearer) softens by 5% of its rank-1 value.
  • A support that adds projectiles, chains or pierces (Branching, Leap, Through the Ranks) gives an overflowing chance: +100% for each one it adds at rank 1, and +35% per rank above.
  • A trigger's chance below 100% grows by 10% of its rank-1 value, up to 100%.
  • A trigger that always fires (On Block, On Parry) rests 10% of its rank-1 cooldown less instead.
  • Areas, ranges, counts, limits, durations, the cooldowns of effects, costs, capacity and eitr reserve stay as they are, except where a gem makes one its benefit (Heavy Impulse, Rain Underfoot, Circle of Malice).
value at rank r = value at rank 1 × (1 + 10% × (r − 1)) drawback at rank r = drawback at rank 1 × (1 − 5% × (r − 1)) overflowing chance at rank r = 100% × added at rank 1 + 35% × (r − 1) cooldown at rank r = cooldown at rank 1 × (1 − 10% × (r − 1)), for a trigger that always fires

An uncut gem's rank comes from the level of the creature or chest that drops it: 1 + ⌊level ÷ 15⌋, at most 5.

Rank Creature level From 1 0–14 Meadows 2 15–29 Meadows 3 30–44 Black Forest 4 45–59 Swamp 5 60+ Swamp

Right-click an uncut gem to open its cutting window: Uncut Trigger Gem cuts into any trigger, Uncut Effect Gem into any effect, curse or aura, Uncut Support Gem into any support. The gem gets the uncut gem's rank. The same uncut gem can instead raise one gem of its kind, in the bag or on the board, by one rank, up to its own rank.

items.title: Rules
items.text:
• Gems leave the board only out of combat.
  • One gem item goes on the board once; two gems of the same kind can both be there.
  • Right-click a gem in the bag to put it into the first free open cell.

items.title: Where glyphs drop
items.text:
Glyphs drop from chests, elite enemies and bosses; ordinary enemies drop none. Each kill or chest rolls once, at its source's chance; a hit gives one glyph, picked by weight among those its biome has opened. A glyph opens in its first biome and stays open after it. The biome is the one the loot's level belongs to; a boss without a level counts as its own biome.

Source Chance of a glyph Boss 50% Elite enemy, 2★ or more 12% Elite enemy, 1★ 6% Dungeon chest 10% Chest above ground 3%

items.title: Veins
items.text: Veins are placed once per world: each 128 m square of a biome may get one, at the chance in the table. A vein stands on free ground, not in water or lava, on slopes up to 35°, away from ore and locations and never within 40 m of a building; when its spot is taken it moves up to 20 m within its biome. A whole vein gives its ore in one stack.

items.title: Smelting
items.text: Every special ore smelts 1:1 into its alloy in an ordinary Smelter: 2 Coal and 30 s per ore, up to 10 ore at once.

items.title: Unusual ore
items.text:
Unusual ore: each unit of ordinary ore a deposit drops may bring one unusual ore of its metal beside it, rolled once per unit; the ordinary ore is kept.

Ordinary ore May bring Tin Ore Heavy Tin Ore 2% Wind Tin Ore 0.5% Scarlet Tin Ore 0.25% Copper Ore Thunder Copper Ore 2% Runebearing Copper Ore 1% Arrow Copper Ore 0.5% Scrap Iron Bog Scrap 2% Frost Iron Ore 0.5% Hot Iron Ore 0.25% Silver Ore Barrow Silver Ore 2% Whisper Silver Ore 0.4% Flametal Ore Hot Iron Ore 3%

Inside a Blight Mist, ordinary tin ore comes out as Scarlet Tin Ore, and heavy tin and wind tin veins give it instead of their own ore.

The Miner's unusual ore chance works per hit: a hit on ordinary ore may knock out one more random unusual ore of the same metal, picked by the chances above (not from tin inside a Blight Mist); on a special vein it adds to the extra yield chances for more of the vein's ore.
