items.title: Unbound Charge
items.text:
Keystone · Strength and Dexterity · Charged Attacks · Show on tree

+25% chance to double all charged-attack effects×0.5 damage

items.title: Keyword: Unbound Charge
items.text: Roll once for the original charged attack. On success, double its charge-granted numerical bonuses and additional-effect counts, including echo, aftershock and phantom-strike payloads. This is not a second use of the attack. Input permissions, target rules, costs and delays do not double.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Charged attack: something charges your next weapon attack, and the next melee or ranged attack you release spends it, hit or miss (spells only with Charged Casts). One charge waits at a time; it doesn't stack or expire.

charged attack: + 25% increased damage, added to your other damage increases, and rows that work with charged attacks apply

A source charges again only 2 s after it last charged the attack (critical hits: 1.2 s). After any charge, every source also waits the shorter of its own cooldown and 3 s (cut by cooldown reduction and recovery). A perfect dodge ignores both cooldowns, but can't charge an attack that's already charged.

With Dash Punch, a charged fist or unarmed attack dashes to the target under your aim; one that isn't charged stays in place.

What charges the attack. Each source needs the passive or mastery option that grants it:

Charges the attack when Granted by an alternative attack hits an enemy Second edge you activate a trinket Flash Response you cast a spell Spell Primes the Strike you cover 25 m running on the ground or levitating, while no charge waits Giant's Run-Up you jump Leap Before the Blow you land a critical hit with an attack Critical Charge you parry a hit Ready Answer you start a dodge roll (a perfect dodge charges it even on cooldown) Rolling Charge

With Choose the Spend, only alternative attacks spend the charge; with Alternate Leads, alternative attacks don't spend it.

Unbound Charge: rolled once when the charge is spent. On success the attack gets 50% increased damage instead, and every row that works with charged attacks counts twice.

Hit splash: a charged attack's first hit on an enemy also hits every other enemy within 3 m × (1 + area of effect increases), for your splash share of its damage.

With the other mechanics: Combat and building.

items.title: Burial ships
items.text:
A Sealed Ship is a drakkar on land, held by chains under a glowing seal. Its cargo lies sealed inside, guarded by the dead: wake them, beat every wave and the final guardian, then accept the gifts.

A ship can appear in any newly generated zone of land (1.8% per zone; never at sea). It is marked on the map once a player comes within 80 m.

A ship's level is the level of the land it stands on (its biome's level). Its guardians are undead of that level and drop nothing; the gifts take the ship's level.

items.title: Cargo
items.text:
Each ship carries one of six cargos, all equally likely; the cargo decides the gifts.

Ship Gifts Rolls Bonus Warrior's Ship Weapons and shields (a unique now and then) 4–6 — Guardian's Ship Armour (a unique now and then) 4–6 — Smith's Ship Metals and materials 5–8 — Runecarver's Ship Currency 4–6 — Seafarer's Ship Coins, then gear or currency at even odds (currency can be a treasure map) 2–4 plus coins Jarl's Ship Rings, belts and trinkets (a unique now and then) 5–7 +50% rarity

The rolls are multiplied by the quantity of the gifts: your chest item quantity and the ship's danger add to it; your chest loot rarity adds to their rarity.

items.title: Smith's Ship
items.text:
Each roll of the smith's cargo is one stack of a metal or material, among the ones the ship's level reaches; the most advanced one is twice as likely.

Item Amount From level Copper 6–12 19 (Black Forest) Tin 6–12 19 (Black Forest) Bronze 4–8 19 (Black Forest) Iron 4–9 43 (Swamp) Silver 4–8 77 (Mountain) Black Metal 4–8 97 (Plains) Carapace 4–9 130 (Mistlands) Flametal 3–6 181 (Ashlands)

Coins (seafarer's ship): 15–30 coins, grown by one part per 40 levels of the ship.

items.title: Dangers
items.text:
A ship has a danger at 35% (one of four, all equally likely). A danger adds 25% rarity and 15% quantity to the gifts (Call of the Barrow: 30% quantity).

  • Funeral Embers: marked ground flares before each wave
  • Call of the Barrow: two guardians in the last wave
  • Cold Trail: guardians leave brief trails of frost
  • Torn Chains: ghostly chains sweep the ground after a warning

items.title: Waves
items.text:
A ship holds 3 waves of the dead, 4 at 20%. "Wake the guardians" starts them; the next wave rises 4 s after the last of the previous one falls, at marked spots.

The first wave has 4 dead for one player, each wave after it one more; every other player within 50 m adds 50% (rounded), up to 12 a wave.

Wave Players: 1 Players: 2 Players: 3 Players: 4 Wave 1 4 6 8 10 Wave 2 5 8 10 12 Wave 3 6 9 12 12 Wave 4 7 10 12 12

The last wave brings the guardian: one more for every 2 extra players, two with Call of the Barrow. Guardians have at least two stars; the other dead roll their stars as usual.

items.title: The gifts

items.title: Merchants
items.text: Three merchants of their own and the finds of Valheim's traders: gear for coins, a gamble by kind, and gifts.

items.title: Ragn Bone-Lot
items.text:
Random equipment of a chosen kind

Ragn's stall stands in the wild: the world is split into squares of 10 × 10 zones, and each square has a stall at 25%, in one of its zones (never at sea). It is marked on the map once a player comes within 300 m. His level is the level of the land his stall stands on.

Pick a kind of equipment and pay: the bundle is opened after paying, with a random base of that kind among the ones open to you at his level (as with gear drops). "The bundle is opened after paying. Level and odds come from this stall."

Rarity Share Common 50% Magic 35% Rare 14.5% Unique 0.5%

When the kind has no unique at his level, the unique's share goes to rare. Trinkets are magic at most: their rare share goes to magic. Ragn has no stock to renew.

items.title: Prices
items.text:
A bundle's price is the base price of its kind, grown by 4% of it per level of his place, rounded to 5 coins:

items.title: Sigrid Far-Road
items.text:
Travelling pedlar: ready goods for gold

Sigrid comes to an active base of your world: beds within 40 m of each other are one base, and a base is active while someone has slept there within 3 days. After a pause of 5 days (before her first visit and after each), each day she comes at 25%. She stops 30–60 m from the base and leaves on the in-game day after the day she came, even with players nearby.

Her whole stock has the level of the highest place any player of the world has reached, or of her stop when that is higher. Every good is one copy for everyone: what is sold is gone.

Her nine goods, rolled when she arrives (gear whose recipe nobody has opened is left out, as with gear drops):

Goods Count Base price Gear, magic or better, of different bases 3 90 (rare ×2.5, legendary ×6) Currency 3 30 a piece, +50% per tier above the first Materials 2 each its own price a unit (below) Treasure map 1 300

Her materials are only ones a player of the world has held: she tries up to 6 times for one, and otherwise sells one of her early goods instead (Flint ×10–20, Leather Scraps ×10–20, Deer Hide ×5–10, Resin ×10–20).

Materials cost a price a unit of their own, the same at every level (any other material: 3):

Prices grow by 2% per level of her stock and are rounded to 5 coins:

items.title: Keeper of Forgotten Sagas
items.text:
Six sagas of the fallen. He gives one away.

He offers unique items of his place's level, all free: "Choose one saga to keep. The others fade with him. A gift for everyone: only one is given." He offers one for every 2 uniques his place's level can give, at least 3 and at most 6. They are drawn by the uniques' weights from the global unique pool, each of another kind where he can (weapon, armour, ring, belt, trinket, jewel). He appears only where at least six uniques can be his.

There is one Keeper in a world. He first appears 1000–3500 m from the start, then, once his gift is taken and every player is farther than 80 m (at least 30 s after the gift), he vanishes and appears again 2000–3500 m from his last place, never within 500 m of a base or a ward. He is marked on the map once a player comes within 500 m.

items.title: Haldor, Hildir and The Bog Witch
items.text:
Valheim's traders also sell random gear of the kind that drops from creatures, under their "Finds" tab: 6–8 items, new every 3 in-game days, at the level of the land the trader stands on. Each find is a random kind of equipment: a unique at 5% when the kind has one at that level, else rare at 40% and magic otherwise. "One copy for everyone: you get exactly this item" A find whose recipe you have not opened stays locked: "Not open to you yet: learn the materials of its recipe"

A find costs Ragn's price for its kind (see above) times 2.5 (magic), 4 (rare) or 10 (unique).

items.title: Selling to merchants
items.text:
Haldor, Hildir and The Bog Witch buy from you under a sell tab beside their finds, and so does the room merchant of the Halls of Oaths. They pay a set price, whatever the item's level:

Goods Pays Magic item, jewel or skill gem 3 Rare item or jewel (a rare skill gem too) 8 Unique item 25 A rune or other currency of tier 1 (uncut gems and chisels too) 1 A rune or other currency of tier 2 (uncut gems and chisels too) 2 A rune or other currency of tier 3 or higher 3

Skill gems sell by their rarity, as magic when they have none; common gear, materials and food don't sell. Equipped items, items in the equipment rows, locked cells, quest items, room items of the halls and treasure maps are never offered. Rare and unique items, gems and currency of tier 3 or higher ask for a second click.

Each merchant pays out of one purse shared by all players: 200 coins, filled again when its stock renews, and the coins players pay it are added to it. A sale it can't pay for is refused.

items.title: Rune of Renewed Trade
items.text:
Rune of Renewed Trade

Renews the stock of the chosen merchant

It renews the stock of a merchant at once: the room merchant of the Halls of Oaths, Sigrid, or the finds of Haldor, Hildir and the Bog Witch. Ragn refuses it, and the rune is not spent: "Ragn sells by chance: he has no stock to renew"

items.title: Treasure maps
items.text:
A treasure map is a scrap of a real map of your world with a red cross on it. Right-click it to read it, find the place, dig away the earth with a pickaxe and open the Buried Chest beneath. Each map has a kind: the kind decides what the chest holds.

A torn scrap of an old map: real shores, hills and a red cross. Use it to read. Dig at the cross with a pickaxe; only the bearer of the map can open the chest.

items.title: Where maps drop
items.text:
A treasure map is a currency drop of chests, dungeon chests, elites, bosses (weight 240 in the currency roll, from item level 1); plain creatures never drop one. How a drop's currency is chosen is on the loot page. A map leads to a land of the level it dropped at.

Sigrid Far-Road sells one on every visit, and the currency of burial ships can hold one too.

items.title: Extra maps from the crafting tree
items.text:
Two clusters of the crafting tree add a chance of an extra treasure map: one (Timber) from elites and bosses you kill, one (Forge) from chests and dungeon chests you open. The chances add up.

items.text:
A map's kind is rolled when it drops, by the weight of each kind. A map of a kind is named by its kind and its land ("Weapon Treasure Map · the Swamp") and its icon shows the kind; its tooltip says what the chest holds.

items.title: What the chest holds
items.text:
The chest's level, shown as the map's reward level, is the level of the land the treasure lies in: its biome's level (or an arena's).

The chest rolls a boss's loot of its level many times over and keeps only the items of its kind, with 150% increased rarity of its own; your chest item quantity and chest loot rarity add to it. When the chest is opened, its items come out 2 at a time.

What each kind keeps (a treasure map itself is never kept):

  • Weapon maps: weapons, bows among them, and unique weapons.
  • Armour maps: helmets, chest and leg armour, capes and shields, and unique ones.
  • Jewellery maps: rings, belts and other utility items, trinkets.
  • Jewel maps: tree jewels that are not unique.
  • Skill gem maps: skill gems.
  • Currency maps: currency of every kind but skill gems and jewels.
  • Rune maps: runes and great runes.
  • Alloy and glyph maps: alloys and glyphs.
  • Halls room maps: rooms of the Halls of Oaths.
  • Unique Treasure Map: exactly one unique item of the chest's level (when there is none at that level, one of the uniques of the lowest level).

items.title: Opening the chest
items.text:
The chest lies buried under the cross: "Dig away the earth over the lid". "Only the bearer of its map can open it": the player who carries the unread map opens it, and the map becomes a "Read Treasure Map". A map whose place could not be found reads "The ink has run: this map leads nowhere"; a map from another world reads "This treasure lies in another world".

When a map was spent on a chest that stayed shut, the player who spent it can open the chest.

Data from Path of Valheiman 6.0.12, extracted 2026-11-13.
